Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.
Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!
If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.
Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!
As a Design Verification Engineer at Lightmatter, you will find yourself at the heart of a dynamic, interdisciplinary team. Your role will involve close collaboration with our digital design experts, using UVM testbench techniques to rigorously verify their designs. Your responsibilities will include working alongside photonic and analog designers, gaining a deep understanding of their innovative designs, and applying Real Number Modeling (RNM) and AMS verification methods. This critical function ensures the integrity of their work. We are hiring at multiple levels.
Your interaction with the Architecture team will be crucial in comprehending system requirements and spearheading performance verification. This role offers a unique platform to enhance your skills across a spectrum of areas including UVM, AMS modeling, mixed-signal verification, post-silicon validation formal verification, emulation, and both performance modeling and verification.

Responsibilities
• Define and enhance the DV methodologies required for integrated digital, analog, and photonic devices with a strong emphasis on emulation for design verification.
• Create and execute test plans to ensure high-quality tapeouts that meet functional and performance goals, while leveraging emulation where appropriate.
• Collaborate with architects, DV engineers, digital designers, and analog/photonics designers to define validation flows.
• Create reusable and scalable test bench components that enable efficient and effective verification.
• Close coverage and finish all DV signoff requirements, with a focus on leveraging mixed signal simulations to achieve high coverage metrics
• Work on block level and full chip design verification.
• Integrate analog design IPs from vendors and internal teams and develop verification environments for simulation and emulation.
• Work with analog design engineers to create behavioral models for analog designs and with digital design engineers to integrate models/testcase/checkers into upper levels

Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
• Minimum of 8 years of design verification and SystemVerilog experience
• 2+ years of experience in Python
• Expertise in developing with the UVM library
• Experience with simulators such as Xcelium, ModelSim, Questa, or VCS
• Strong problem solver and collaborator

Preferred Qualifications
• Master’s degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience with 6 years of relevant experience
• Experience with post-silicon validation and debug
• Experience with AMS verification

Position Overview
We are seeking a hands-on ASIC Design Verification Lead to own verification execution for complex, high-performance networking silicon. This role is a senior technical leadership position focused on driving verification strategy, infrastructure, and closure, while remaining deeply involved in day-to-day hands-on verification work.
This is not a people-manager-only role. The ideal candidate is a highly technical verification leader who has personally taken chips to tape-out, understands how verification breaks late in the cycle, and can drive functional correctness, coverage closure, and tape-out readiness in a fast-moving startup environment.

Responsibilities
Verification Strategy & Execution
• Define and own block-, subsystem-, and chip-level verification strategies
• Develop and maintain scalable verification environments using SystemVerilog and UVM
• Drive execution from test-plan definition through coverage and bug closure
• Ensure verification readiness as a gating requirement for tape-out
Hands-on Verification Development
• Write and review high-quality testbenches, sequences, checkers, and scoreboards
• Develop constrained-random, directed, and stress tests to validate complex corner cases
• Actively debug functional failures across RTL, testbench, and simulation environments
Coverage & Quality Ownership
• Define functional, code, and assertion coverage goals
• Analyze coverage results and identify verification gaps
• Provide clear, actionable feedback to RTL designers to improve design and test quality
Cross-Functional Debug & Collaboration
• Partner closely with RTL, architecture, physical design, and firmware teams
• Drive root-cause analysis of functional, performance, and integration issues
• Support gate-level, timing-aware, and power-aware simulations as required
• Partner and support emulation and post silicon validation of the ASIC design
Full-Chip & Pre-Silicon Validation
• Lead full-chip verification planning, execution, and closure
• Support emulation and acceleration environments where appropriate
• Ensure clean handoff to silicon bring-up teams with high confidence in design correctness
Execution Discipline & Technical Leadership
• Establish and enforce verification checklists and quality gates
• Track verification progress and risk, proactively escalating issues
• Lead by technical authority and hands-on contribution rather than coordination alone
• Continuously improve verification methodology, infrastructure, and best practices

• Proven track record of taking at least one complex ASIC to tape-out with direct verification ownership

jobs.description:
Role Overview
We are looking for a talented Senior Formal Verification Engineer to define, own, and scale the formal verification effort that hardens Velaura's next-generation Physical AI SoC. You will apply formal methods to the hardest correctness problems in the design, working with architects, RTL, and verification teams to prove correctness exhaustively and reach coverage that simulation cannot. We welcome engineers who enjoy reasoning rigorously about complex hardware, taming state-space explosion, and finding the corner-case bugs no one else can.

Responsibilities
• Own and drive formal verification for complex SoC blocks—CPUs, control processors, floating-point units, vector/SIMD engines, and datapath-heavy designs.
• Write high-quality SVA properties and formal testbenches to prove functional correctness, including end-to-end and datapath-equivalence checks.
• Apply full proofs, bounded model checking, assume-guarantee reasoning, and abstraction to close proofs on deep-state designs.
• Debug counterexamples and drive convergence on hard proofs using abstraction, constraints, and decomposition.
• Verify floating-point and arithmetic units for IEEE-754 compliance using formal datapath and equivalence checking.
• Build reusable formal apps: connectivity, register/CSR, deadlock/liveness, X-propagation, and control-path proofs.
• Define constraints and modeling assumptions, and prove them consistent and non-over-constraining.
• Drive formal coverage closure and integrate it into the overall verification signoff plan.
• Partner with architects, RTL, and simulation teams to align on what to prove formally versus in simulation.
• Maintain automated infrastructure, scripting, and CI hooks for formal regression and proof tracking.
• Use modern AI-assisted verification and debug workflows to improve productivity and coverage.
• Contribute to a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

jobs.description:
Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced verification leader to help verify and deliver Velaura's next generation Physical AI SoC. You will work closely with architects, RTL engineers, software engineers and system teams to establish confidence in the correctness, performance, reliability and safety of the design, from individual RTL blocks through complete hardware and software systems running real workloads.
This role leads system level verification. You will own the SoC verification plan and carry it through sign off and into tape out, covering boot and root of trust, clock and reset topology, low power behavior, and the IO and memory subsystems. You will set technical direction for a small team while staying hands on in the environment yourself.

Responsibilities
• Own the SoC level verification strategy, plan and execution for the Velaura Physical AI SoC.
• Build and lead a team of SoC verification engineers, setting technical direction and reviewing their work.
• Define the SoC verification architecture and environment, and stay hands on in the code.
• Coordinate verification across boot and security, clock and reset, low power, and the IO and memory subsystems.
• Define sign off criteria and coverage goals, and drive closure through tape out.
• Track and report verification progress, coverage and risk to engineering leadership.
• Work with architecture, RTL, DFT, firmware and software teams on system level correctness and pre silicon bring up.
• Partner with CAD and infrastructure teams on simulation, emulation and regression capacity.

Required Qualifications
• 12 or more years in design verification, including significant SoC level experience.
• Experience leading SoC verification across multiple projects through sign off and tape out.
• Experience building and leading a team of verification engineers.
• Experience with SystemVerilog, UVM, C and C++ and coverage driven verification at system level.
• Experience managing simulation flows on CPU based SoCs such as ARM or RISC-V.
• Knowledge of IO and memory subsystem IP such as PCIe and LPDDR5 or LPDDR6.
• Experience verifying boot and root of trust, clock and reset topology, and low power behavior at system level, including CDC, RDC and UPF based flows.
• Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence engineering leaders across disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with HW and SW co verification and pre silicon software bring up.
• Experience with emulation and FPGA prototyping at SoC level.
• Experience with one or more of ISO 26262, IEC 61508, IEC 61511 or ISO 13849.
• Experience verifying QoS, latency sensitive or real time systems.
• Experience with post silicon bring up, debug and root cause analysis.
• Experience building a verification team at an early stage company.
• Familiarity with robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles or industrial automation systems.
• Experience using AI assisted verification workflows to improve productivity and coverage.

Why Velaura?
Velaura is building next-generation compute technology for cloud, edge, and Physical AI. Our solutions will enable robots, autonomous systems, drones, and other intelligent machines to operate efficiently in the physical world.

We’ve raised over $100M from world-class investors including Softbank, Threshold Ventures, Lux Capital, and DCVC, and secured multi-million-dollar customer contracts across multiple markets.
The salary range for this position is $120,000–$225,000+ annually. Actual compensation depends on experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

Design Verification at Mythic:
At Mythic, our Design Verification (DV) team is central to ensuring the correctness and reliability of our novel digital dataflow architecture, which includes a sophisticated scheduling subsystem, high-performance interconnect fabric, and advanced DMA engines that work together with our Analog Compute Engines to accelerate AI workloads. DV engineers collaborate closely with RTL design, architecture modeling, custom analog IP, compiler, emulation, and post-silicon teams to ensure the full system operates as intended.
Because today’s AI workloads are too large and intricate to be fully verified in hardware alone, our team takes creative and rigorous approaches—combining simulation, modeling, and innovative verification strategies—to prove that neural networks will function correctly and efficiently. We welcome engineers at all levels of experience who are eager to tackle challenging verification problems and contribute to the success of our breakthrough AI hardware.

Responsibilities

• Development of test plans and coverage plans.
• Testbench development and execution using UVM or other advanced DV methodologies.

• Collaborate with RTL designers and architects to verify subsystems such as scheduling fabrics, interconnects, DMA engines, and memory controllers.

Requirements
• Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science.
• 8+ years of industry experience developing verification testbenches.
• Knowledge of verification methodologies (UVM or similar).
• Solid understanding of computer architecture, including datapaths, memory hierarchies, and interconnects.
• Experience verifying one or more of the following: scheduling subsystems, high-performance interconnects, DMA engines, or memory subsystems.
• Understanding of Verilog, SystemVerilog, and UVM.
• Proven track record of first-pass silicon success.
• Strong communication skills, both written and spoken.

Preferred Qualifications

Intel's Client AI Architecture team is seeking an Deep Learning Hardware Engineer to help shape future generations of Intel's Neural Processing Unit (NPU) architecture for AI PCs, Edge AI, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and multimodal foundation models.
In this role, you will work at the intersection of AI, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design to optimize AI workloads and drive innovations in next-generation AI acceleration technologies. You will collaborate with architecture, software, compiler, and machine learning teams to develop high-performance, power-efficient AI solutions for Intel client platforms.
The ideal candidate has experience developing, optimizing, or deploying AI workloads on NPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, or related computing architectures. Experience with Intel NPUs, OpenVINO, AI software stacks, compiler technologies, AI inference optimization, and hardware-software co-design is highly desirable.

• Contribute to the design and optimization of neural compute and AI accelerator architectures.

Company:
Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

Job Area:
Engineering Group, Engineering Group > ASICS Engineering

General Summary:
We are seeking a highly skilled engineer to enable highly optimized mapping of AI workloads to Qualcomm’s next generation system-technology solutions for the slowing Moore’s law era. The focus is on identifying the system and technology bottlenecks for the state-of-the-art and emerging AI workloads e.g. the mixture-of-experts (MoE), multi-tenant vector databases, multimodal physical AI etc.. The E2E system KPIs for mapping these emerging AI workloads include the power, performance and TCO of the entire system encompassing the SoC, memory and networking.
The primary role of the candidate is to map the workloads using both internal and external tools to Qualcomm’s next-gen AI accelerator systems and carry out what-if scenarios of optimizing different underlying components e.g. SoC, memory, networking and other technology features for the best power-performance-TCO trade-off. The candidate also needs to ensure which AI workloads are relevant for the different business units (BUs) from datacenters to physical AI to computing devices.
To drive these technologies the person will collaborate with high-level representatives across functional teams (e.g. Architecture, product management, SW teams) to enable an implementation strategy that meets system requirements.
The preferred location for this position is San Diego, CA. Qualcomm's Santa Clara and Austin locations may also be considered. The position is expected to comply with the company's onsite work policy and is not eligible for remote work.

The Central Hardware Systems (CHS) HW Sys design team designs cutting-edge Hardware systems and printed circuit boards across Qualcomm's most strategic platforms — spanning DataCenter, Server, Connectivity, Compute, and R&D. The Principal Engineer will lead hardware embedded system development of data center platforms built on Qualcomm SoCs, from test platforms, R&D, accelerator / CPU cards to multi-card server systems and rack-level designs. These platforms serve as production products, reference designs, verification and validation systems, software and firmware development vehicles, and SoC test platforms.
The systems are high-power and high-density, with very high-speed interconnects. They include high-bandwidth memory (LPDDR/HBM/DDR5), PCIe Gen5/Gen6 and CXL, high-speed Ethernet scale-out fabrics (400G/800G), 112G+ SerDes, multi-phase power delivery at very high current, advanced thermal solutions including direct liquid cooling, and board management and security subsystems. The role works closely with server ODMs and Qualcomm's SoC, software and systems teams to deliver platforms and sys designs that perform, scale and are reliable in production.
• Lead hardware projects and design teams from architecture and requirements phases through design, validation, bring-up, system integration and production.

• Lead system-level design optimization and resolution of complex electrical, optical, mechanical, compatibility, compliance, manufacturing and cost issues.
• Provide technical leadership for advanced analysis including signal integrity, power integrity, feasibility, characterization and hardware validation.
• Collaborate across diverse cross-functional teams including IC design, software, systems, test, Customer Engineering, manufacturing and operations to deliver high-quality production solutions.
• Coordinate design handoff to ODM and provide support for ODM design and production.
• Serve as a technical authority and mentor, providing design reviews, technical direction and guidance across multiple engineering teams and projects.
• Drive innovation, intellectual property, process improvement and future product capabilities by applying technical expertise

Company:
Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

Job Area:
Engineering Group, Engineering Group > ASICS Engineering

General Summary:

Hardware System Design Engineer, Senior Staff
Location: San Diego, CA (100% On-Site) Employment Type: Full-Time
Level: Senior or Staff — final level and title will be determined based on the selected candidate’s experience and demonstrated scope of impact.

Position Summary
You will be part of a hardware design team that builds high-performance FPGA-based emulation platforms. You will own the board design process — schematic capture, PCB stack-up, PCB layout, power and signal integrity simulation, BOM management, and design verification testing — while driving system-level architecture in close partnership with customers and software/firmware teams. You will work cross-functionally to evaluate design trade-offs, direct lab technicians through system installation and debug, and partner with design, CAD, and manufacturing teams on prototyping, testing, and production support. Candidates with broader scope and a track record of technical leadership may be considered at the Staff level, where they will additionally define system architecture across multiple boards/platforms, set design methodology and standards for the team, serve as the primary technical interface with customers, and mentor senior and junior engineers.

Key Responsibilities
• Own the board design lifecycle: schematic capture, PCB stack-up (26+ layers), PCB layout, BOM management, and design verification testing.
• Drive system-level architecture in collaboration with customers, software, and firmware development teams.
• Perform power and signal integrity simulations for 10 Gbps+ SERDES and high-speed I/O, from model extraction through simulation, reporting, and recommended design changes.
• Lead or support FPGA board design (Xilinx and/or Altera), including DDR3/DDR4/DDR5 discrete memory subsystems.
• Direct lab technicians on system installation, bring-up, and debug of boards and multi-board systems, including root-cause investigation of the most complex issues.
• Collaborate with mechanical, PCB layout, and manufacturing teams to ensure designs are optimized for signal integrity, manufacturability (DFM), and reliability.
• Author and maintain design documentation (HDDs, pinout tables, design review packages) to support cross-team alignment and program reviews.
• Serve as a key or primary technical point of contact with customers and cross-functional stakeholders on system architecture decisions and trade-offs.
• Support factory/production builds and new product introduction (NPI) activities as needed.

Required Qualifications & Experience
Core Board Design & Signal Integrity
• Experience with the board design process including schematic capture, PCB stack-up, PCB layout (26+ layers), BOM management, and design verification testing.
• Experience with FPGA board design (Xilinx and/or Altera).
• FPGA HDL coding experience.
• Experience with 10 Gbps or higher SERDES board designs.
• Experience performing power and signal integrity simulations for 10 Gbps+ signals, including various I/O analyses, using established methodologies from model extraction through simulation, reporting, and recommending design changes to address failing simulations.
• Experience with circuit and layout guidelines, high-speed design concepts, signal integrity, and transmission line theory.
• Experience with DDR3/DDR4/DDR5 discrete component board designs.
• System architecture design experience; candidates for the Staff level should have experience defining architecture across multiple boards/platforms.
Protocols, Tools & Test Equipment
• Familiarity with I2C, JTAG, UART, SPI, SD Card, PCIe, and eMMC protocols.
• Familiarity with test equipment including oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers.
• Board- and system-level bring-up and debug experience.
• Basic Linux/Unix experience.
• Familiarity with Microsoft Office, Mentor Graphics DxDesigner/Expedition, Vivado, Quartus, HyperLynx, Sigrity PowerSI/PowerDC, ADS, Ansys HFSS, and SPICE.
Collaboration & Professional Skills
• Proven ability to work with cross-functional teams (mechanical, PCB layout, manufacturing, software/firmware, program management) to deliver high-quality boards and systems on schedule.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present design trade-offs and simulation results to technical, customer, and cross-functional audiences.
• Demonstrated ability to work independently, prioritize competing priorities, and drive tasks to closure with minimal supervision.
• Experience mentoring or providing technical guidance to junior engineers; Staff-level candidates should also demonstrate experience mentoring senior engineers and leading design reviews.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice to Have)
• Power supply design experience.
• Experience with signal integrity and PDN (power delivery network) simulations.

Help build the optical connectivity that moves AI forward.
AI performance depends on more than compute—it depends on how efficiently data moves. At Marvell, you’ll help turn advanced coherent DSP technology into high-performance hardware platforms that enable faster, more power-efficient optical networks.

What You Can Expect
Join the team developing hardware platforms for Marvell’s coherent digital signal processors (DSPs), critical enablers of high-speed transmission over fiber-optic networks. Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

AI’s next breakthrough depends on more than compute—it depends on how efficiently data moves. As AI clusters scale out across racks and data centers, optical connectivity becomes essential to delivering the bandwidth, power efficiency, and performance these systems demand.

jobs.description:
Change the World! Love your job!
Come join our Connectivity Automotive Applications team and help drive the development and adoption of our wireless microcontrollers for both Car Access, Wireless Battery Management Systems (WBMS) and Tire Pressure Monitoring Systems (TPMS). As a RF Hardware Applications Engineer, you will be an integral part of our team leading the revolution of connectivity in automotive use cases, and specifically be involved in our team focused on Bluetooth Low Energy, Ultra-wideband (UWB) and our TI WBMS Protocol. We’re searching for an experienced hardware applications engineer who has the passion and excitement to grow in this position, innovate, and take an active role in supporting automotive customers as they design, ramp and manufacture their products with TI connectivity products inside. This position requires someone who enjoys working in an international environment and brings a positive “can do” attitude to their objectives.
In this position you’ll work with closely with TI customers to determine their design challenges and partner with them on creating solutions, design optimization and improving their products. This can involve travelling to the customer and working together on-site to solve any issues and deliver presentations both in-house and onsite. You will spend hands-on time in a world-class RF lab tackling technical challenges and delivering innovative development solutions that support our products and drive revenue. Become a part of the team redefining the way we connect with our vehicles!
This role is responsible for application support for low power connectivity solutions. Key responsibilities include:
• Answer customer questions and supporting design-in activities for released products. This includes:
• Forum and email questions from customers
• Schematic and Layout Review of customer application
• Debug of customer problems by re-creating issues in our evaluation boards and/or customer boards
• On-site support on customer boards as required
• Plan, design, develop and characterize RF development kits (LaunchPads), EVMs and RF reference designs
• Test and optimize RF performance on customer HW and reference designs in our high-end RF lab, including schematic and layout reviews of customer application
• Electromagnetic (EM) simulations and analyses of designs (balun, filtering, transmission lines, impedance matching)
• Develop and optimize RF PHYs
• Be a technical expert on RF/HW and provide technical support to the company's sales staff and customers
• Develop technical documentation including application notes, user guides, design notes and white papers.
• Internal and customer training, through training events like FAE summits and TI Tech Days or written materials, like application notes, journal papers, or IEEE papers.
• Interface with various cross-functional teams (e.g. Designers, System Engineering, Software Engineering, Business)
• Establish key relationships with our customers and field team

• Solid hardware and software debugging skills
• Strong technical background, with the ability to produce high quality technical documentation

jobs.description:
Power Semiconductor System Applications — PV & Energy Storage
Your role
The Staff Hardware Engineer will independently lead hardware development for power semiconductor system applications — including residential and commercial PV systems, energy storage systems (ESS, including balcony ESS and utility-scale PCS), PV optimizers, and battery chargers. This role requires hands-on capability in power electronics schematic and PCB design, solid understanding of common power converter topologies, and the ability to drive hardware projects from concept through prototype, validation, and production release. The ideal candidate will work closely with firmware, testing, and product teams to deliver robust, standards-compliant hardware solutions for the renewable energy market.
Key responsibilities in your new role
• Independently design and develop power electronics schematics using industry-standard tools (Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or equivalent) for power semiconductor-based systems, including PV inverters, ESS power conversion systems, PV optimizers, and battery chargers.
• Independently perform PCB layout design with proper consideration for high-voltage creepage and clearance, thermal management, and signal integrity.
• Design and validate power converter circuits based on common topologies (e.g., LLC, CLLC, DAB, NPC, HERIC, B6, Totem-pole PFC), selecting appropriate power semiconductors (SiC MOSFETs, IGBTs, diodes), gate drivers, and passive components to meet application requirements.
• Select and evaluate components — power semiconductors (SiC/IGBT), gate drivers, current/voltage sensors, DC-link capacitors, magnetic components — based on datasheet analysis, loss calculation, and application-specific trade-off studies.
• Build, test, and debug hardware prototypes: perform PCB assembly and rework, set up test configurations, conduct functional testing, power-stage characterization, and design verification.
• Conduct design verification activities including thermal testing, efficiency measurements, and reliability validation under worst-case operating conditions.
• Collaborate with firmware engineers on control loop tuning, system bring-up, and hardware-software co-debugging; work with the testing team on compliance certification (safety, grid code).
• Create and maintain comprehensive design documentation, including schematics, BOM, design rationale notes, test reports, and design guidelines for reuse across projects.
Your profile
Qualifications and skills to help you succeed
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Automation, or a related field, with at least 2 years of relevant work experience in power electronics hardware design. Outstanding fresh graduates with strong hardware project experience are also welcome to apply.
• Proven ability to independently design power electronics schematics and PCBs using industry-standard EDA tools (Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or equivalent), with a portfolio of completed hardware designs.
• Familiar with at least one or two common power converter topologies — such as LLC, CLLC, DAB, NPC, HERIC, B6, or Totem-pole PFC — including their operating principles, design considerations, and practical implementation trade-offs.
• Solid understanding of power semiconductor devices (SiC MOSFETs, IGBTs, Si diodes), gate driving techniques, loss analysis, and thermal management for high-power-density designs.
• Hands-on laboratory experience with test equipment including oscilloscopes, differential probes, current probes, power analyzers, electronic loads, and programmable power supplies.
• Familiarity with relevant safety and design standards (e.g., IEC 62109 for PV, GB/T 34120 for ESS grid connection) is a plus.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, self-driven attitude, and ability to manage multiple tasks independently in a fast-paced environment.
• Good communication skills in both English and Chinese; ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional and cross-regional teams.

Preferred Qualifications (Bonus)
• Experience with wide-bandgap (SiC/GaN) power converter design and high-switching-frequency PCB layout techniques.
• Knowledge of embedded MCU peripheral integration (PWM, ADC, communication interfaces) for digital power control systems.
• Prior experience in the renewable energy industry (PV inverter, energy storage PCS, or EV charger product development).

jobs.description:
Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) provides rack-scale AI infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. By collaborating with hyperscalers and ecosystem partners, Astera Labs enables organizations to unlock the full potential of modern AI. Astera Labs’ Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates CXL®, Ethernet, NVLink, PCIe®, and UALink™ semiconductor-based technologies with the company’s COSMOS software suite to unify diverse components into cohesive, flexible systems that deliver end-to-end scale-up, and scale-out connectivity. The company’s custom connectivity solutions business complements its standards-based portfolio, enabling customers to deploy tailored architectures to meet their unique infrastructure requirements. Discover more at www.asteralabs.com.

Overview
Astera Labs Inc. is seeking an experienced and self-driven Hardware Lab Engineer to join our dynamic team in developing world class connectivity products for AI infrastructure.

Job Description
This role will work closely with firmware, system validation, quality, and product engineers to support silicon bring-up, characterization, and debug activities through hands-on lab execution. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of circuits, hands-on experience with PCBAs and silicon test environments, and the ability to work on complex, open-ended tasks with minimal oversight.

Key Responsibilities
• Setup and maintain test environments for silicon validation and characterization. Configure and update hardware, software, firmware, and applications. Replicate BKCs.
• Conduct hands-on testing of silicon devices including PCIe Gen5/6/7, CXL, Ethernet, and other high-speed interfaces
• Install and configure servers, including FW, BIOS, OS, and network
• RMA intake/triage: inspection, electrical verification, screening (including CSAM inspection), and prioritization
• Manage logistics and communications with external labs
• Organize, track, and distribute lab equipment, hardware, and peripherals
• Ad hoc PCBA rework and soldering of fine-pitch SMD components
• Develop, document, and maintain lab procedures

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field
• 5-12+ years of hands-on experience in lab environments supporting silicon validation or hardware development
• Proficiency with high-speed test equipment (oscilloscopes, protocol analyzers, BERTs, multimeters)
• Experience with high-speed interface testing (PCIe, CXL, DDR, Ethernet, or SerDes)
• Strong programming skills in Python for test automation
• Familiarity with Linux operating systems and command-line tools
• Demonstrated experience coordinating with third-party testing laboratories and managing logistics, including sample shipping, chain of custody, and scheduling
• Strong organizational skills for managing multiple RMA cases simultaneously and prioritizing based on severity/impact

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with post-silicon validation of ASICs, SoCs, or Retimer/PHY products
• Knowledge of analog/mixed-signal circuit testing and debugging techniques
• Experience with JTAG, I2C, SPI, and other embedded interfaces
• Familiarity with PCB design, schematic reading, and signal integrity concepts
• Knowledge of data center systems architecture (servers, AI platforms, networking equipment)
• Understanding of ATE (Automated Test Equipment) systems and production test methodologies
• Experience with defect screening methodologies including visual inspection, electrical testing, and acoustic imaging
• Experience with complete RMA lifecycle management from intake through root cause analysis and corrective action
• Knowledge of common semiconductor failure modes and failure analysis techniques including die attach inspection, delamination detection, void analysis, and crack identification
• Experience with formal compliance testing and industry standards
The base salary range is $160,000.00 USD – $200,000.00 USD. Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions.
We know that creativity and innovation happen more often when teams include diverse ideas, backgrounds, and experiences, and we actively encourage everyone with relevant experience to apply, including people of color, LGBTQ+ and non-binary people, veterans, parents, and individuals with disabilities.

jobs.description:
About the role
Credo is seeking an Senior Optical Hardware Engineer to join our Zero Flap optical module development team at our San Jose headquarters. In this role, you’ll validate and debug optical modules operating at 212.5 Gbps (PAM4) and beyond, applying your expertise in signal and power integrity to ensure optimal performance and readiness for high-volume production. You’ll partner with cross-functional teams and industry partners to advance Credo’s Zero Flap optical products from prototype through mass manufacturing—playing a critical role in shaping the next generation of high-speed optical interconnects.
Base salary range is $140,000 – $210,000 a year. The base salary offer will depend on factors such as education, experience, training, skills, qualifications, and location. This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus, equity and a full range of medical and other benefits.

Why Credo
• Purpose: We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact.
• People: Connection starts within. We collaborate, celebrate wins, and create an environment where everyone can do their best work.
• Possibilities: Our belief shapes what’s next. Our technology powers the most reliable and energy-efficient connections around the world – and our team powers new products and markets that come next.

Responsibilities
• Review PCB requirements, interfaces, and constraints with mechanical, firmware, optical, and manufacturing teams, and review PCB layouts, including component placement, stack-up design, high-speed routing, controlled impedance paths, and SI/PI-driven layout strategies.
• Perform PCB bring-up, debugging, and characterization using oscilloscopes, VNAs, and power analysis tools, and review SI/PI simulations and modeling reports (channel analysis, PDN optimization, high-speed data path modeling) for 1.6Tbps+ module architectures.
• Support NPI and mass production, ensuring manufacturability, yield, reliability, and DFM compliance, and partner with manufacturing teams on production readiness and timely issue resolution.
• Coordinate electrical-optical system integration for high-speed modules, aligning PCB architecture with optical engine requirements; define electrical interfaces for optical components (drivers, TIAs, DSPs/Coherent ASICs, lasers, photodiodes) to ensure signal integrity across the optical chain; and support integration of optical subassemblies (ROSAs, TOSAs, Coherent Optical Engines), including connector selection, power delivery, and high-speed interface routing.
• Collaborate with optical, mechanical, packaging, and supplier teams to co-optimize PCB designs for thermal paths, mechanical constraints, fiber routing, and optical engine placement; debug electrical-optical performance issues (modulation errors, link margin, thermal drift, eye diagrams, interface compatibility); develop system-level test plans validating performance against industry standards (IEEE, OIF, MSAs); and ensure seamless integration across firmware, DSP/ASIC behavior, power regulation, clocking, and optical performance.

Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
• B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Optoelectronics, Optics, or Applied Physics, with 7+ years of relevant experience.
• Familiarity with industry standards governing optical modules (IEEE, QSFP-DD, OSFP, CMIS).
• Proficiency with PCB design and analysis tools.
• Hands-on experience with high-speed optical and electrical test equipment, and familiarity with optical alignment and manufacturing-floor equipment, with strong skills in analyzing alignment data.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience developing PCBs for 800Gbps or 1.6Tbps optical transceiver modules.
• Familiarity with optical component manufacturing technologies and the industry landscape.
• Experience leading and contributing to cross-functional teams.

About Credo
Credo’s mission is to transform connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions. Our high-speed copper and optical interconnect products deliver industry-leading power and performance at up to 1.6T to meet the ever-expanding data infrastructure demands of AI.
Our product portfolio includes ZeroFlap (ZF) Active Electrical Cables (AECs) and ZF optical transceivers, OmniConnect memory solutions, and a suite of retimers and DSPs for optical and copper Ethernet and PCIe, all leveraging the PILOT diagnostic and analytics software platform. Credo innovations enable our customers to connect the systems that connect the world.

jobs.description:
Sandisk’s Product Security Engineering & Assurance (PSEA) organization is seeking highly motivated Product Security Engineers - Hardware/Firmware specializing in security considerations for Client and Enterprise storage products (SSDs) that incorporate hardware and firmware components. This role will partner closely with firmware, hardware, Platform Security, validation, and product teams to strengthen security across Sandisk products through product security assessments, security readiness assurance, PSIRT support, technical risk mitigation guidance, and product security enablement. The ideal candidate combines strong technical depth in embedded systems and firmware with practical product security experience and the ability to influence engineering teams toward scalable, risk-informed security outcomes. This role requires strong technical judgment, hands-on engagement, and the ability to communicate complex cybersecurity topics to engineering, business, and customer stakeholders.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Product Security Engineering & Enablement
• Partner with firmware, hardware, and product teams to strengthen cybersecurity considerations across product lifecycles.
• Provide technical guidance on implementation of security requirements and security controls for hardware and firmware-based products.
• Evaluate product security posture and implementation effectiveness with a security lens, identifying potential attack paths, control gaps, and risk areas.
• Help product teams prioritize practical mitigations based on product risk, exploitability, and business objectives.
• Support product teams in balancing cybersecurity rigor with product delivery objectives and business priorities. Security Risk
Assessment & Threat Modeling
• Facilitate product security risk assessments and support threat modeling activities across firmware-driven products.
• Assess product security risks across: authentication and authorization mechanisms, firmware update protections, secure boot and trust anchors, cryptographic protections, debug and manufacturing access controls, provisioning and lifecycle security mechanisms.
• Participate in technical reviews to evaluate security implementation effectiveness and identify opportunities for risk reduction.
Security Readiness & Assurance
• Support product security readiness activities by evaluating implementation effectiveness, security evidence, and residual product risk from an assurance perspective.
• Assess security posture and implementation effectiveness related to: authentication and authorization mechanisms, firmware update protections, secure boot and trust anchors, cryptographic protections, debug and manufacturing access controls, provisioning and lifecycle security mechanisms.
• Evaluate security artifacts and technical evidence including: threat modeling outputs, SAST and static analysis findings, SBOM and dependency risk visibility, fuzzing and penetration testing outcomes, vulnerability remediation activities, security validation evidence.

jobs.description:
Apple is seeking a Reliability Engineer to join our Mac Hardware Reliability team! In this role, you’ll collaborate with diverse hardware teams to ensure our products are not only durable and reliable, but also built to exceed expectations. From early concepts to field returns, you’ll lead cross-functional teams, design innovative reliability tests, and drive continuous product improvements. The Azure Memory & Storage (AMS) Commodity Quality and Validation Engineering (CQVE) team is responsible for ensuring storage device quality, reliability, and compliance before deployment at Azure scale.

Other Requirements

• 8+ years of experience working with enterprise storage technologies, including HDDs, SSDs, SAS, SATA, PCIe or NVMe devices, with demonstrated expertise in storage architecture, performance, reliability, and failure analysis.
• 5+ years of experience leading development of validation strategies, qualification programs, test methodologies, or automated test frameworks for hardware products.
• Proven experience leading cross-functional technical initiatives and influencing product quality, validation requirements, or engineering roadmaps across suppliers, partners, and internal engineering organizations.
• Meaningful hands-on experience working with server platforms and storage subsystems.

requirements: 3+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience

jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
Amazon Leo is building a next-generation satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity around the world. Success requires engineers who can think beyond individual components and understand how every subsystem comes together to form a reliable spacecraft.
As a Spacecraft Hardware Engineer on the Bus Structures team, you will help define the physical architecture of our spacecraft. Working across Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, RF, Propulsion, Manufacturing, Test, and Systems Engineering, you will develop structural solutions that integrate every subsystem into a cohesive, manufacturable, and flight-ready vehicle.
This role combines structural design with spacecraft integration. You will evaluate complex engineering tradeoffs involving structural performance, manufacturability, thermal interfaces, assembly, transportation, testing, launch vehicle integration, and on-orbit operations to ensure the spacecraft performs as an optimized system rather than a collection of individual subsystems.
Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
• Design and develop spacecraft structural hardware and vehicle architectures.
• Integrate multiple spacecraft subsystems into a cohesive mechanical design.
• Perform engineering trade studies balancing structural performance, manufacturability, mass, cost, schedule, and integration requirements.
• Develop detailed mechanical designs from concept through production.
• Collaborate across Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, RF, Manufacturing, and Systems Engineering.
• Support structural analysis, qualification testing, manufacturing, and launch integration activities.
• Resolve hardware issues through root cause analysis and engineering problem solving.
• Contribute to the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) release process and configuration of flight hardware.
A day in the life
As a Spacecraft Hardware Engineer, you'll spend your day solving multidisciplinary engineering problems that span the entire spacecraft. One meeting may focus on integrating a new propulsion component into the vehicle, while the next evaluates structural changes needed to improve manufacturability or simplify assembly. You'll participate in design reviews, develop structural concepts, support qualification testing, work with manufacturing teams, and collaborate with engineers across nearly every technical discipline. Every decision contributes to building a spacecraft that is structurally sound, manufacturable, launchable, and ready for years of successful operation in orbit.
About the team
The Bus Structures team is responsible for the physical realization of the spacecraft. Beyond designing the primary and secondary structure, we develop the overall vehicle architecture and ensure every subsystem integrates into a cohesive spacecraft. We provide the system-level perspective necessary to balance structural performance, thermal performance, RF accommodations, manufacturability, assembly, transportation, launch vehicle integration, testability, and operational success.
As the primary vehicle integration authority, our team works across every engineering discipline to optimize the spacecraft as a complete system rather than individual subsystems. We also own the final mechanical configuration through the Product Lifecycle Management release process, ensuring the authoritative vehicle definition remains consistent throughout development and production. - 3+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience
• Experience with CAD tools and engineering documentation.
• Experience working on multidisciplinary engineering teams.
• Understanding of mechanical design fundamentals, structural analysis, materials, and manufacturing processes.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills. - Experience developing aerospace, spacecraft, defense, automotive, or other highly integrated hardware systems.
• Experience with structural analysis, finite element analysis, or mechanical testing.
• Experience with product integration, systems engineering, or multidisciplinary design trade studies.
• Experience supporting hardware through qualification, manufacturing, and production.
• Familiarity with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems and engineering change processes.
• Experience balancing competing technical requirements across multiple engineering disciplines.

jobs.description:
Amazon LEO is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon LEO will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.
As a High Speed Digital Design Engineer on the Customer Terminal team, you will own high-speed digital interfaces — DDR, Ethernet, and SerDes — for next-generation terminal products. You'll drive component selection, schematic design, signal integrity simulation, and lab validation, collaborating across hardware, silicon, and systems teams to deliver robust, cost-optimized designs ready for high-volume manufacturing.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
• Select and qualify high-speed interface components (connectors, retimers, PHYs, ESD protection) balancing performance, cost, availability, and manufacturability
• Own schematic capture for high-speed digital subsystems — define net topologies, termination schemes, and interface pin assignments in collaboration with PCB layout engineers
• Own signal integrity analysis for high-speed interfaces (DDR, PCIe, Ethernet, USB, MIPI) from architecture through production, including simulation, design rule development, lab validation, and correlation
• Perform channel modeling and simulation using EM tools (ANSYS HFSS/SIwave, Keysight ADS, Cadence Sigrity, Hyperlynx) to verify interconnect performance meets silicon requirements
• Participate in schematic and layout design reviews, providing signal and power integrity feedback to ensure designs meet performance and cost targets
• Validate high-speed interfaces in the lab using oscilloscopes, VNAs, TDRs, and high-fidelity probing techniques. Correlate measurements back to simulation models
• Collaborate with silicon, RF, antenna, thermal, mechanical, power, and systems teams to close budgets and solve problems within real-world product constraints
• Support board bring-up, debug, and root-cause analysis of SI/PI-related failures
• Support designs through qualification, production ramp, and high-volume manufacturing
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
• Knowledge of CAD software like Orcad and Allegro
• 3+ years of experience in high-speed digital interface design and/or Signal Integrity simulation/validation - Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
• Experience designing cost-optimized, high-volume consumer electronics
• Experience with Power Distribution Network (PDN) design, simulation, and validation
• Experience with SI/PI co-simulation for mixed-signal applications
• Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production

Automation & Controls Engineer, Launch Hardware Production (Starship)
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

Automation & Controls Engineer, Launch Hardware Production (Starship)
This role owns the controls that build Starship.
You will design, commission, and operate the automation behind production systems. A 24-lane, 750,000 sq ft Starship Refurbishment facility (Gigabay) built to assemble & refurbish Starship at rate. Industrial air separation units upstream of the propellant farms. Heat shield tile manufacturing. This team owns that controls scope end to end. The work runs from a blank cabinet and a P&ID to a plant that stays up. You will specify instrumentation, program PLCs, pull in the data, commission the equipment, and then live with it in production. When a lane stops, a cold box trips, or a furnace drifts, you find it, fix it, and change the system so it does not happen again.
This position is based in Cape Canaveral, FL (Kennedy Space Center).

RESPONSIBILITIES
• Design, build, and commission the controls for a 24-lane Gigabay: production tooling, lifts, fixtures, factory services, and the data layer the floor uses.
• Bring industrial air separation units online and keep them running. Own the instrumentation, interlocks, and control narratives for compression, cold box, distillation, storage, and transfer into the propellant farms.
• Own controls for heat shield tile manufacturing: thermal process equipment, material handling, inspection, and the data that ties process settings to tile quality.
• Stand up new equipment from first power-on through rate production, then own uptime once it is live.
• Develop and upgrade data acquisition and control systems as the factory, the air separation plant, and the tile line change.
• Maintain the operational capability of control-voltage (<60V) electrical systems once activated.
• Turn sensor and PLC data into something operators and responsible engineers can act on the same shift.
• Support controls technicians and the mechanical, facilities, and process engineers who depend on these systems.
• Design hardware and work methods that cut cost, install time, and the time it takes to recover a down line.
• Analyze data to judge the health of electrical and process systems, and use it to drive the next change.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS
• Bachelor's degree in physics, electrical engineering, or computer engineering.
• 6+ months of experience working with data acquisition systems (internship or project experience qualifies).

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
• Demonstrated ability to design, implement, commission, and troubleshoot industrial control and data acquisition hardware.
• Hands-on PLC and industrial network experience: Modbus, PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, or equivalent.
• Experience commissioning process or factory equipment and supporting it after it is in production.
• Working knowledge of instrumentation in classified and cryogenic service (NFPA 70, NFPA 70E; Class I, Division 1 and Division 2, or IEC equivalent).
• Fundamental understanding of the equipment behind a plant: sensors, valves, drives, analyzers, power distribution, grounding, and signal integrity.
• Familiarity with mixed-signal electronics, schematic capture, and PCB design, verification, or validation where custom hardware is the right answer.
• First-hand programming experience beyond ladder: enough software to move data out of a controller and into a tool the factory can use.
• Knowledge of high-reliability build, test, and documentation practices.
• Excellent written and verbal communication. You will write the narrative, then go stand at the panel with the technician.
• Strong work ethic, a bias for finishing, and the ability to change roles quickly in a high-paced environment.
• Ability to drive work with incomplete information and to keep several systems moving at once.
• Passion for making the hardware that makes flight rate possible.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting, and working in cramped positions and small openings.
• Ability to climb stairs and ladders regularly throughout the day.

Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. Starlink also designs, builds, and delivers high-volume consumer hardware that allows users to connect to these satellites within minutes of unboxing, as well as our advanced gateways that we deploy regionally throughout the world. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.
As an Electrical Design Engineer on the Starlink team, you will have complete ownership over the development of millions of customer-facing products and devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.). Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. SR. HARDWARE DESIGN ENGINEER - ELECTRICAL, SATELLITE PAYLOAD (STARLINK)
The Starlink team designs, builds, and operates the world’s most advanced communication network. Comprised of over ten thousand satellites in low Earth orbit and dozens of antenna installations on the ground, this system delivers broadband internet to more than ten million customers around the world. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computer and electric propulsion systems to their advanced phased array antennas and the ASICs which enable them. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact, and as we continue to upgrade and scale the system, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.
As an Electrical Design Engineer on the Starlink Payload Engineering team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life- cycle of the hardware that enables this connectivity, and sits at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal, software, and antenna/RF engineering. Our team specializes in the design of industry-leading phased array and parabolic antennas, as well as the fully custom networking, compute, and modem hardware which drive them. Common design elements include high power mixed-signal ASICs, cutting edge PAM4 SerDes, fully custom RF front ends and antenna elements, highly reliable and dense power conversion and distribution, extreme temperature environments, custom copper and optoelectronic interconnect, and tight electromechanical/thermal integration designed for mass manufacturing. Engineers are deeply involved with their products from concept to deorbit. Typical ownership spans block diagrams and high-level concept of operations definition, requirements capture, part selection and schematic capture, PCB layout oversight, signal and power integrity analysis, supply chain and vendor engagement, hardware bring up and qualification, production test definition, troubleshooting and failure analysis, review of hardware performance on orbit, and the incorporation of lessons learned and design improvements for the next generation.

• Rapidly develop high-reliability electronics for satellites and spacecraft.
• Drive system trades, requirements capture, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, hardware bring-up, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, test, and on-orbit performance of complex electrical designs
• Get hands-on and support hardware through production, satellite integration, and flight
• Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test, supply chain, silicon design, RF and antenna, ) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware
• Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another STEM discipline
• 5+ years of experience design/analysis ofcircuits, electronic products, or hardware

• Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or similar engineering degree
• 5+ years of electronic product experience designing hardware from concept through production; strong emphasis on full life-cycle development of new hardware products and not small incremental updates to legacy hardware
• 3+ years of experience designing and implementing mixed-signal circuit boards from concept through production using processors, FPGAs, Ethernet, multi-GHz Serdes, DRAM interfaces (DDR4, LPDDR5, etc.), I2C, SPI, RFsignal chains, operational amplifiers, analog to digital and digital to analog converters, and power supply components

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, MECHANICAL HARDWARE & FASTENER STARSHIP
Every Starship flight depends on thousands of bolts, nuts, screws, fittings, and joining hardware performing flawlessly under extreme load, temperature, and vibration. In this role, you own that commodity end to end: the manufacturers who form and machine, the heat treat and chemical processing that finish, and the quality systems that ensure reliable function. SpaceX is building a supply chain that can scale from prototype to high-cadence flight hardware without sacrificing reliability. We need an engineer who will be the extreme owner of fasteners and hardware — and who will push suppliers, processes, and designs until quality, cost, and rate all win.
This is a hands-on, highly technical role. You will spend time on shop floors, at heat treat and coating lines, in metrology labs, and in design reviews — not just in meetings. The ideal candidate has manufacturing depth, a genuine interest in mechanical fasteners, and the urgency to solve hard problems that protect the flight manifest.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Own the mechanical hardware commodity for Starship: Fasteners (bolts, nuts, screws), Dynamic Hardware (springs, bearings, rod ends) and Fluid Control (fluid fittings, filters), and related joining devices — from supplier selection through rate production.
• Serve as the primary technical point of contact for assigned parts and suppliers; resolve emergent manufacturing, quality, and capacity issues that threaten the build or flight schedule.
• Lead new product introduction (NPI) and work transfers for fastener and hardware products: qualify suppliers, validate processes, and ramp production to aggressive takt times.
• Drive production part approval and process validation (PPAP, FAIR, capability studies) so every critical characteristic is controlled and proven before hardware reaches the vehicle.
• Lead containment on nonconforming hardware; define scope with engineering, quality, and production; execute disposition (rework, repair, use-as-is, or scrap); and prevent recurrence.
• Root-cause defects at the supplier, at SpaceX, or both — including heat treat, plating/coating, thread forming/rolling, machining, forging, material certs, and dimensional/GD&T escapes.
• Partner with design and manufacturing engineering to improve part designs, specifications, and process callouts for manufacturability, lead time, cost, and defect reduction.
• Assess supplier capability and capacity (equipment, tooling, personnel, quality systems) and develop underperforming suppliers or dual-source/re-source when required.
• Work with procurement to identify, vet, and grow exceptional fastener and specialty hardware suppliers who can meet aerospace quality and SpaceX rate.
• Become the go-to expert on your parts and processes; own supply-chain-related defects and drive them to zero escapes.
• Serve as SpaceX’s SAE representative; attend technical committee meetings and advocate for company positions on fastener, hardware, and related standards.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline
• 1+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, or supplier development

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
• Hands-on familiarity with mechanical fasteners and joining hardware (bolts, nuts, screws, studs, washers, pins, springs, fittings, inserts, etc.)
• Experience with fastener or precision hardware manufacturing processes: cold heading/forging, thread rolling or cutting, machining, heat treatment, surface finishing, plating/coating, passivation, and secondary ops
• Familiarity with destructive and nondestructive inspection methods relevant to fasteners and hardware (e.g., hardness, tensile, fatigue, magnetic particle, fluorescent penetrant, dimensional metrology)
• Working knowledge of aerospace and industry fastener/material standards (e.g., NAS, AN, MS, ASTM, AMS, NASA/JSC, ISO)
• Experience assessing supplier technical capability and capacity (equipment, process control, operations, and people)
• Knowledge of supplier quality frameworks: PPAP, APQP, FAIR, control plans, PFMEA, MSA
• Experience with quality systems (AS9100, ISO 9001) and high-reliability or high-volume production environments
• Proven ability to drive root cause and corrective action using structured methods (8D, 5-Why, fishbone, Pareto) and statistical tools (capability, DOE, SPC; Minitab or equivalent a plus)
• Comfort reading engineering drawings, including GD&T, material callouts, and special process requirements
• Experience with CAD and drawing creation or revision collaboration with design engineering
• Experience implementing process improvements, automation, or advanced inspection in manufacturing or quality
• Strong written and verbal communication; ability to influence suppliers and internal stakeholders under schedule pressure
• Knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methods

As a Hardware Security Engineer focusing on Hyperscaler Security, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring Cisco's next-generation platforms and custom Hyperscaler hardware architectures adhere to rigorous security, trust, and resilience standards. You will analyze sophisticated systems from the high-level architecture down to component-level silicon, guiding multi-functional engineering teams and external partners to deliver robust, secure hardware solutions.

Who You Are
You are a collaborative hardware engineer with a background in hardware design, low-level architecture, and security principles. You enjoy translating complex technical standards into practical engineering requirements and partnering across disciplinary boundaries to solve complicated hardware security problems. You communicate technical concepts clearly through engineering documentation and multi-functional collaboration, and you thrive when driving multiple parallel technical initiatives in a dynamic environment.
• System-to-Silicon Security Analysis: Evaluate system-level hardware designs, schematics, board architectures, and component datasheets to identify threat vectors, vulnerabilities, and compliance gaps.
• Standards & Regulatory Translation: Interpret, apply, and establish requirements aligned with emerging industry standards and compliance frameworks, including NIST SP 800-193 (Platform Firmware Resiliency), NSA CNSA 2.0 (Post-Quantum Cryptography / CNSA Suite), the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), and internal Hardware Cisco Secure Development Lifecycle (HW-CSDL) mandates.
• Technical Guidance & multi-functional Influence: Serve as a technical advisor, providing clear, actionable security requirements and architectural design guidance to product teams, hardware design engineers, firmware/BIOS teams, and third-party vendors.
• Documentation & Technical Collateral: Author hardware security requirements, review checklists, threat models, compliance white papers, and engineering specifications for internal and external consumption.
• Multi-Stream Project Engagement: Participate in and manage multiple concurrent security evaluations, design reviews, and compliance workstreams across diverse hardware programs.

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field with 7+ years of relevant experience (or Master's degree with 4+ years of experience, or PhD with 1+ year of relevant experience).
• Prior background in hardware development (e.g. reading and interpreting system-level schematics, block diagrams, component datasheets, PCB design or review, or register-level hardware documentation).
• Prior background in hardware security fundamentals, such as Hardware Root of Trust (RoT), Secure Boot, hardware and firmware resiliency, cryptographic primitives (symmetric/asymmetric encryption, hashing, digital signatures), or secure key storage.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with crafting, implementing, or evaluating hardware-rooted attestation architectures and device identity mechanisms (e.g., SPDM, TCG DICE, etc.).
• Experience with Hyperscaler and cloud platform architectures (e.g., OCP specifications, OpenBMC, Caliptra, OpenTitan, OpenPRoT, etc.).
• Experience implementing industry standard security IP or developing novel HW security solutions (e.g. FPGA bitstream security, secure microcontroller architectures, HW RoT, bus encryption).
• Experience with hardware threat modeling or hardware security analysis (e.g., fault injection, side-channel analysis, JTAG/debug security).
• Background in hardware security frameworks and standards, such as NIST SP 800-193, NSA CNSA 2.0, TCG DICE / TPM, or global cybersecurity regulations (e.g., EU CRA).

Meet the Team
The Product Operations team within the Core Routing Business Unit (CRBU) plays a critical role in delivering Cisco’s next-generation hardware products at scale. Working at the intersection of engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing, the team ensures seamless product lifecycle execution—from new product introduction to high-volume production and customer delivery. With a strong focus on reliability, efficiency, and operational excellence, the team drives impact across global operations and enables successful product outcomes.

Your Impact
Cisco Hardware Engineers are at the forefront of building the technology that powers the future. By balancing innovative design with rigorous IEEE standards, you will play a meaningful role in taking products from initial concept to high-quality production.
In this role, you will work across a broad spectrum of the Cisco portfolio—including system and board design, signal integrity, power design, and validation. Whether you are defining industry standards as an architect or ensuring product reliability as a solution integrator, you will collaborate with multi-functional teams and external partners to optimize performance, cost, and quality. We are looking for engineers who are eager to challenge the status quo and drive innovation through research and practical application. Responsibilities include:
• Silicon, Package & Board Characterization: Validate high-speed channels from silicon die through the PCB interface using advanced time-domain and frequency-domain techniques. Partner with layout engineers to optimize routing and define manufacturing test requirements.
• PCIe Gen 6 Validation: Execute physical layer compliance and characterization for PCIe Gen 6/7 protocols, utilizing PAM4 signaling, multi-tap equalization, and advanced clocking architectures.
• High-Speed Measurement Execution: Operate precision lab instrumentation, including multi-port Vector Network Analyzers (110GHz+), high-bandwidth Oscilloscopes, Bit Error Rate Testers (BERTs), and Time Domain Reflectometers (TDRs).
• Measurement-to-Simulation Correlation: Extract S-parameters and utilize tools such as Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS, or Cadence Sigrity to correlate lab data with simulation models. Drive root-cause analysis based on these findings.
• Root-Cause Debugging: Troubleshoot complex signal and power integrity anomalies, such as insertion/return loss, crosstalk, jitter, and noise, to ensure robust product performance.
• Lab Automation: Develop and maintain Python or MATLAB scripts to automate instrument control, streamline data collection, and process complex validation datasets.

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of related experience, or Master’s degree and 3+ years of related experience, or PhD plus 1+ years of related experience.
• 5+ years of applied experience with VNA to measure multiport S Parameter (insertion loss, return loss and X talk)
• Capability to set up TDR setups to locate impedance discontinuity, trace routing mismatches, structural damage in PCB, cables and connectors

Meet the Team
The Outshift by Cisco team is one of the Cisco’s most visible innovation organizations, driving the next generation of transformative technologies and business opportunities. You will collaborate with some of the company’s most forward-thinking researchers, engineers, and technology leaders. Within the Outshift Quantum Research team and Quantum Labs, we are pioneering the design and development of practical, scalable, and efficient quantum networking technologies — foundational building blocks for the future Quantum Internet. Our multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers is dedicated to advancing the state of the art in quantum networking, distributed quantum systems, and quantum-enabled applications.

Your Impact
Cisco Quantum Research is seeking a skilled Principal Hardware Engineer to support our Quantum Experimental Team in a role that is central to the physical realization of Cisco's deployable quantum hardware platforms.
• You act as the primary technical authority responsible for delivering integrated, rack-mounted quantum systems directly to customer data centers and research facilities, directly driving customer satisfaction and site-acceptance timeline success.
• You will unify disparate engineering domain outputs—including precision control electronics, RF/microwave distribution, thermal management, optical/photonic routing, and fiber management—into a cohesive, manufacturable, and serviceable rack architecture.
• You will serve as a critical link between the scientific research team and the program management function, ensuring that hardware assembly and test activities are performed with precision.
• Architect scalable, manufacturable rack solutions by integrating electrical, RF/microwave, thermal, optical, and fiber-optic subsystems.
• Lead the design, integration, and deployment of rack-level quantum systems for customer data centers and research environments, including EIA-310-compliant rack infrastructure, PDUs, UPS integration, grounding, electrical isolation, thermal management, and environmental monitoring systems.
• Ensure compliance with global electrical and safety standards, including UL, CE, and IEC requirements.
• Optimize system layouts for performance, reliability, serviceability, and efficient cable and fiber management.

Meet the Team
Cisco Silicon One (#CiscoSiliconOne) is a business organization with a long track record of building complex and high-performance Silicon ASICs. Our silicon devices drive the world’s most complex networks and carry over 90% of IP traffic. Cisco Silicon One is the only unifying silicon architecture in the market that enables customers to deploy the best-of-breed silicon from Top of Rack (TOR) switches all the way through web scale data centers and across service provider, enterprise networks, and data centers with a fully unified routing and switching portfolio.
We are a highly specialized ASIC team with experts in all aspects of advanced IC package design and heterogeneous system integration. Our substrates use the latest 2.5D fanout technologies for large-scale integration, using the latest signaling and data transfer technologies. Come join us and take part in shaping Cisco's ground-breaking solutions by designing, developing and testing some of the most complex ASICs being developed in the industry!
The Cisco Service Provider Routing Hardware Engineering team develops next-generation hardware by adhering to IEEE standards and industry best practices. Our engineers drive innovation across the full product lifecycle, serving as IP architects, creators, and solution integrators who manage products from concept to production.
