jobs.description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.
Security is a paramount focus for Google's Tensor SoC and Pixel, especially with advancements like Gemini and Gen AI. As a Software Engineer on our team, you will develop innovative systems security solutions at the hardware-software interface, protecting users and their data across Google's flagship devices and services. By applying your software skills to write robust code, you will manage complex security challenges, address emerging threats, and implement next-generation security features.
Google's mission is to organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful. Our team combines the best of Google AI, Software, and Hardware to create radically helpful experiences. We research, design, and develop new technologies and hardware to make computing faster, seamless, and more powerful. We aim to make people's lives better through technology.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

jobs.description:
Like Google's own ambitions, the work of a Software Engineer goes beyond just Search. Software Engineering Managers have not only the technical expertise to take on and provide technical leadership to major projects, but also manage a team of Engineers. You not only optimize your own code but make sure Engineers are able to optimize theirs. As a Software Engineering Manager you manage your project goals, contribute to product strategy and help develop your team. Teams work all across the company, in areas such as information retrieval, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking, security, data compression, user interface design; the list goes on and is growing every day. Operating with scale and speed, our exceptional software engineers are just getting started -- and as a manager, you guide the way.
With technical and leadership expertise, you manage engineers across multiple teams and locations, a large product budget and oversee the deployment of large-scale projects across multiple sites internationally.
The Laptops and Tablets (L&T) Platform bringup team designs and builds the system software, device driver and hardware enablement firmware that powers Google’s Chromebooks and Googlebooks, directly enabling the next generation of secure, reliable, and fastest-booting computing experiences.
In this role, you will be working at the intersection of hardware and software, you will drive open-source initiatives while partnering closely with major SoC and hardware vendors. Your team translates complex silicon capabilities into seamless experiences used by millions of people globally.
The Platforms and Devices team encompasses Google's various computing software platforms across environments (desktop, mobile, applications), as well as our first party devices and services that combine the best of Google AI, software, and hardware. Teams across this area research, design, and develop new technologies to make our user's interaction with computing faster and more seamless, building innovative experiences for our users around the world.

As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you lead complex, multi-disciplinary engineering projects using your engineering expertise. You plan requirements with internal customers and usher projects through the entire project lifecycle. This includes managing project schedules, identifying risks and clearly communicating them to project stakeholders. You're equally at home explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical trade-offs in product development with engineers.
Using your extensive technical and leadership expertise, you manage projects of various size and scope, identifying future opportunities, improving processes and driving the technical directions of your programs.
Fuchsia is Google's open-source, capability-based operating system, built on the Zircon microkernel and shipping on Google Nest devices. Our Security, Privacy, and Firmware program makes sure every product built on Fuchsia boots and updates reliably, is secure by design, and respects user privacy. The work spans the bootloader and verified boot, trusted execution environments, OS hardening, vulnerability response, and privacy reviews for every platform release. We partner with Android, product teams, Legal, and silicon vendors, and much of the platform is developed in the open at fuchsia.dev.
Fuchsia is a modern, open source operating system that is simple, secure, updatable, and performant. It’s a general purpose OS, designed to power an ecosystem of hardware and software, and provides core operating system functions like system resource management, a driver framework, and software abstractions.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $163000 - $236000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
Learn more about benefits at Google.
• Define the multi-quarter roadmap for operating system security, privacy, and firmware, translating ambiguous requirements into structured programs with clear milestones, risk ratings, and exit criteria.
• Manage programs for the platform's boot and update stack including verified boot, over-the-air updates, and recovery while aligning release milestones and firmware readiness with external silicon vendors.
• Direct security and privacy launch approval processes for platform releases and new hardware form factors by coordinating privacy design reviews, audits, and legal alignment to ensure secure, on-time delivery.
• Guide vulnerability management and incident response initiatives from the OS level down to vendor firmware, tracking findings against severity-based SLOs and upstreaming patches to reduce measurable risk.
• Cultivate strategic cross-organizational partnerships to deliver platform capabilities like hardware-backed key management, while building scalable tooling (including AI-assisted workflows) and streamlining review processes to improve organizational efficiency.
• Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
• 5 years of experience in program management.
• Experience in security engineering standards and practices, or managing security or privacy programs.
• Experience working with operating systems, firmware, or embedded software development teams.
• 5 years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.
• Experience with platform security technologies such as secure/verified boot, bootloaders, trusted execution environments (TEEs), hardware-backed key management, SELinux, or fuzzing.
• Experience managing technical programs for bootloaders or system firmware (e.g., U-Boot, UEFI, Android bootloaders), including flashing, A/B and over-the-air (OTA) updates, recovery, and production signing-key processes.

jobs.description:
Overview
Microsoft Silicon and Cloud Hardware Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Skype, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate, motivated engineers to help achieve that mission. As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and HW infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance.
The Firmware Center of Excellence is responsible for Hardware/Firmware for Azure Infrastructure. We are working on the next generation Hardware/Firmware for server, silicon and rack infrastructure with a focus on innovation in firmware technology to secure Azure infrastructure for Microsoft and their customers.
We are looking for highly motivated Senior Software Engineer - Blade Server BMC Firmware Development, with a background in Firmware architecture & design who can influence the partners and drive end to end (E2E) solutions from concept to production. Experience with Platform & System-on-Chip (SoC) Architecture and Design, bring up of SoC, root causing issues at the intersection of multiple subsystems across firmware and hardware.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
This role will require a minimum of three days in office.

Responsibilities
• Design and architect firmware solutions for Cloud Hardware systems, focusing on system-level E2E design,debugging and troubleshooting.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams including hardware engineers, software developers, validation &integration, and product managers to define firmware requirements and specifications.
• Develop and maintain firmware architecture, ensuring scalability, modularity, and maintainability.
• Develop Security threat models for the platform working with vendors & Security teams.
• Stay up-to-date with industry trends and advancements in firmware technologies, and provide recommendations for improvement.
• Work closely with Microsoft product groups, industry partners and researchers to architect and develop server hardware solutions that meet the requirements for our cloud services platforms at the lowest possible cost of ownership.
• Design and implement firmware modules to support various hardware interfaces, including USB vNIC, SPI, I2C, I3C, PCIe, and other related protocols.
• Provide technical leadership and guidance to internal developers or external partners to deliver serviceable, reliable, and scalable solutions.
• Contribute to product vision and roadmap by bringing innovation to server manageability ecosystem.
Perform system-level debugging and troubleshooting to identify and resolve hardware/firmware-related issues

jobs.description:
Ring is growing in Poland and we are looking for experienced Embedded Software Engineers to join our team in Gdansk. You will work on firmware for IoT devices used by millions of customers worldwide, developing new features and shipping products from concept to production.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will own the design and implementation of firmware subsystems running on resource-constrained hardware. You will work across the full development cycle: architecture, implementation, code review, testing on real devices, and production release. Our team operates with high autonomy and a strong feedback culture.

The ideal candidate:
• Has shipped embedded products to production and understands what it takes to go from prototype to millions of devices in the field.
• Writes clean, maintainable C/C++ for constrained environments and cares deeply about code quality.
• Communicates proactively, raises technical risks early, and drives solutions across teams.
• Thrives in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift as customer needs evolve.
• Is curious about the full stack, from hardware registers to cloud connectivity, and enjoys learning new domains.
Key job responsibilities
• Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware in C/C++ for Ring devices.
• Specify and implement functionality for embedded subsystems (connectivity, streaming, power management, sensors, or security).
• Collaborate with hardware, QA, cloud, and app teams to deliver integrated product experiences.
• Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, and cross-team architecture decisions.
• Debug complex issues across hardware and software boundaries using JTAG, UART, and protocol analyzers.
A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing a code change from a colleague working on a new sensor driver. After your team standup, you spend focused time implementing a feature for an upcoming product launch, testing it on real hardware at your desk. In the afternoon, you dig into a tricky issue that only reproduces on one board variant, tracing it from application code down to a register misconfiguration. jobs.description:
Ring is growing in Poland and we are looking for a Senior Embedded Software Engineer to join our firmware team in Gdansk. You will shape the firmware that runs on IoT devices used by millions of customers worldwide, and you will do it as a technical leader: setting the architecture, raising the bar on quality, and making the engineers around you better.
This is a hands on role. You will still write code and debug hardware. The difference at this level is scope. You will own the technical direction of a significant part of our firmware, decide how subsystems fit together, and be the person other teams come to when a problem crosses a boundary that nobody owns yet. You will take a product from an early idea and an unfinished board through to millions of units in the field, and you will be accountable for the decisions that made it work.
Our team operates with high autonomy and a strong feedback culture. We expect you to disagree with us when you think we are wrong.
Key job responsibilities
• Own the design and implementation of firmware spanning several subsystems, such as connectivity, streaming, power management, sensors, or security.
• Lead your colleagues to deliver high quality C and C++ that will scale with the needs of the business.
• Make architecture decisions that hold up across products, and write them down clearly enough that other teams can build on them.
• Set the technical bar through code review, design review, and the standards you hold yourself to, and empower your colleagues to meet and raise it.
• Mentor engineers, grow the people around you, and multiply what the team can deliver.
• Partner with hardware, QA, cloud, app, and silicon vendor teams to deliver one integrated product experience, and drive the decisions that cross those lines.
• Work with your manager and leadership to shape the firmware roadmap and influence the technical strategy behind it.
• Find and fix the hardest problems we have, including the ones that only reproduce on one board variant, at low temperature, or after eight hours of soak.
• Raise technical risk early, with a recommendation attached.
A day in the life
You start by reviewing a design document and pushing back on a choice that will not hold once a second product picks it up. After standup you write a driver for a new part and test it on the board at your desk. Midday you help the hardware team decide whether firmware can cover a missed power target. In the afternoon you pair on a bug that runs from application code down to a register, and show your colleague how to find it rather than fixing it yourself. You close the day writing to leadership about a schedule risk.
About the team
We build the firmware inside Ring devices, from doorbells and cameras to security products. Our work starts before the hardware exists and continues long after launch, which means we own architecture, bring up, feature delivery, and the health of what is already in customers' homes. jobs.description:
Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building revolutionary robotic systems that combine AI, sophisticated control systems, and advanced electromechanical design to create adaptable automation solutions capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation.
Amazon is seeking a talented and motivated Senior Embedded Firmware Engineer to design, implement, and launch firmware for highly dexterous robotic end effectors. In this role you will own firmware sub-domains independently. The ideal candidate has extensive experience writing firmware to process a wide variety of sensors, control electric motors, and communicate with the larger system, and can work well both independently and in a multidisciplinary team setting.
Key job responsibilities
• Drive communication interface integration at the firmware layer, ensuring robust, deterministic communication between the end effector and the larger robotic system.
• Review vendor firmware deliverables, provide technical direction, and hold vendors to Amazon's quality, coding, and integration standards.
• Author functional requirements, design verification plans, and test procedures; execute designs that meet those requirements.
• Build and test firmware for electromechanical subsystem prototypes and integrated systems, covering sensor processing, motor control, and system communication.
• Support product releases to manufacturing and customer deployments, including production firmware bring-up and validation, working efficiently to support fast-paced development schedules.
A day in the life
Your morning starts with a new sensor module on your desk: the latest prototype from a manufacturing partner overseas. You jump on a call with the vendor's engineering team to walk through their test results, flag an issue you spotted in the data, and agree on a firmware fix they'll turn around overnight. Getting fast iteration cycles on hardware is how this team operates: you don't wait for perfect specs, you get hardware moving and learn from what it tells you.
By mid-morning you're designing the control interface for the end effector: defining how it talks to the rest of the system, what data it exposes, and how it fits into the real-time communication architecture. You sketch the firmware-side changes, then switch to the simulation environment to update the corresponding ROS model so the controls engineer you're working with can test policies against it before hardware arrives. Making things work in sim and on your dev kit in the same day is normal here: the hardware hasn't shipped yet, but that doesn't stop you.
After lunch you pick up a code review from another team. They're building the actuator control framework that your end effector integrates with, and their latest change surfaces a new set of requirements you hadn't considered. You leave substantive feedback, and it reshapes how you're thinking about your own interface design.
You close the day with a quick chat with a teammate on the mechanical design side who's working on a physical sensor model. They want help writing custom firmware to characterize the sim-to-real gap, and you realize it connects directly to the simulation change you made that morning. What started as two separate threads becomes a collaboration. You open a shared design doc and start outlining the approach together.
About the team
We're developing next-generation robotic manipulation capabilities for highly dexterous multi-finger grippers and hands. Our firmware work spans motor control, sensor processing, tactile sensing production firmware, and the tight integration of the robotic end effector with the larger robotic platform. jobs.description:
Amazon Robotics is seeking a Senior Embedded Software Engineer with deep Rust expertise to help lead development of safety-rated sensor processing firmware for one of the world's largest autonomous robot fleets. You will set technical direction for major subsystems of the Safety Perception stack (real-time safety applications, sensor processing pipelines, and system interfaces on heterogeneous multi-core MCU/CPU/GPU platforms) that let robots in Amazon facilities worldwide detect and respond to obstacles safely and reliably. You will own the team's hardest end-to-end problems, framing solutions where the business need is clear but the technical strategy is not, and raise the bar for the engineers around you.
We are looking for a technical leader who is deeply proficient in Rust (or strong in C/C++ and eager to work in Rust), is fluent across the boundary between RTOS and Linux on the same chip, has substantial experience with sensor data acquisition or signal processing, and can architect systems that meet the rigor of IEC 61508 functional safety certification. You will influence beyond your immediate team, shaping designs, resolving escalations, mitigating long-term one-way-door risks, and mentoring engineers, all while collaborating closely with hardware, functional safety, and navigation teams to deliver firmware where correctness is not optional.
Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate is a force multiplier who sets technical direction across teams and raises the bar for associate safety. They will:
• Lead the design and architecture of major safety-rated and non-safety-rated firmware subsystems in Rust on heterogeneous multi-core platforms, where real-time safety code and Linux services coexist on the same chip.
• Set technical direction across the full sensor processing pipeline (driver integration, frame acquisition, point cloud generation, collision detection) and influence peer hardware, safety, and navigation teams.
• Own the team's hardest end-to-end problems, framing solutions where the business problem is known but the technical strategy is not.
• Drive perception features that let robots detect and respond to obstacles under IEC 61508 certification, ensuring data integrity through black-channel diagnostics.
• Raise the technical bar through design and code reviews, and mentor engineers so the team is more reliable because of your presence but does not require it.
• Produce direction-setting design documents and safety analysis artifacts that meet the rigor of third-party certification and witness testing.
• Lead debugging and root-cause analysis end-to-end, from raw sensor data to safety responses, on real robots at test facilities and in production.
• Leverage AI coding assistants as a force multiplier and lead the team to do the same.
A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might spend the morning aligning peer teams around a subsystem architecture in a design review, then head to the test floor after lunch to lead a cross-functional debug with electrical and QA engineers, determining whether an issue is firmware, hardware, or a faulty sensor. That afternoon you profile a pipeline to close a latency budget, then pair with another engineer to unblock their design. Our engineers take complete ownership (from interrupt handlers to CI/CD pipelines to on-site data collection) and frequently enter new areas to meet our customers' needs. As a senior engineer, you help chart where the team goes next.
About the team
The Safety Perception team is a group of passionate embedded software engineers who apply advances in robotics and sensor processing to real-world safety challenges. We write embedded Rust on platforms where correctness is not optional, and we own the full stack: from low-level driver integration to system APIs to the test infrastructure that proves our firmware works. We take our responsibility for safety seriously while challenging ourselves to ship the right product at the performance we need. You will design, implement, test, and debug production NOS software across platform drivers, routing and control-plane state, ASIC programming, observability, and fleet integration. The engineer in this role should be able to work through ambiguous, open-ended technical problems and drive feature development across software, hardware, and vendor boundaries.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

EMBEDDED SECURITY ENGINEER (STARLINK)
At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and serves millions of users worldwide. We design, build, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites and all of the space-ground infrastructure necessary for a constellation of that size. As we scale the constellation to hundreds of thousands of satellites, and become a foundation of global connectivity both on earth (and in space), we are looking for excellent engineers to help us build secure, defensible systems from the ground up.
In this role, you will influence the security of software across our space and terrestrial systems. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:
• Applied cryptography
• Network security
• Operating system security
• Secure/Authenticated boot
• Incident response and adversary detection
• Vulnerability research
• Software Engineering

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Design and build security infrastructure for Starlink, including cryptographic services and other security-critical services
• Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites
• Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this
• Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams
• Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements
• Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

EMBEDDED SOFTWARE ENGINEER, DATA CENTER ENGINEERING (STARMIND)
The Data Center Engineering team designs training and inference compute clusters from first principles, pushing thermal, electrical, and optical systems to the limit of physics. We operate as a highly cross disciplinary team comprised of mechanical, electrical, optical, and software engineers, all working to maximize the efficiency, reliability, and deployment speed of terrestrial computing to serve rapidly scaling demand.
As an Embedded Software Engineer on our team, you will design, validate, and ship code that reliably and autonomously manages hundreds of thousands of coherently connected GPUs. Your software will span the entire hardware stack from individual firmware ICs up through cluster aggregation networking, ensuring our compute fabric operates at peak efficiency and gracefully handles various fault conditions. To empirically define the limit of physics in our computing hardware, you will also work closely with mechanical, electrical, and optical engineers to develop automated hardware test environments for thermal, radiation, and power testing.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Develop highly reliable, real-time software designed to run on compute tray host systems, baseboard management controllers, network switches, and peripheral rack hardware.
• Participate in and lead architecture, design, and code reviews.
• Develop prototypes and manage experiments to prove out key design concepts.
• Develop tools for software development and deployment, data analysis and visualization, and test execution across multiple environments, including hardware-in-the-loop regression testbeds and in-field testing.
• Deploy reliable software, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable).
• Development experience in C, C++, or assembly.
• Experience with application development and distributed systems architecture in a Linux environment.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
• Strong first-principles problem-solving skills and a focus on designing bug-free, maintainable software;
• Strong professional experience writing C, C++ or assembly in a production environment.
• Developed, debugged and deployed software that has been used in real world hardware applications/projects, especially those for high performance computing infrastructure.
• Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.
• Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.
• Experience with networking protocols (UDP, TCP/IP, etc.) and distributed systems.
• Experience in security issues associated with distributed systems and internet services.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
We design, build, and operate the largest AI supercomputers in the world, from the ground up. As a member of the Platform Core team, you will be responsible for the lowest layers of the software stack on the devices setting the pace for how fast we can push the frontier of AI. Our team’s software interfaces directly with the core hardware of the supercomputer and its network fabric.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Build and maintain the lean, high-reliability Linux-based operating system that underpins our supercomputer network fabric and Starlink laser mesh of satellites.
• Write (or rewrite) high-performance device drivers to extract the maximum physical capability from our network and compute hardware.
• Manage deployment, operation, and debugging of our platform in production, including:
• Rigorous resolution and root-causing of anomalies to ensure the system is constantly improving in reliability.
• Developing and constantly improving our tools for observability and configuration management.
• Collaborate with our hardware teams and external partners to design the next generation of supercomputer hardware and then bring up our OS and software stack on it.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable).
• Hands-on system programming experience in C or C++.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
• Deep knowledge of the Linux kernel and its networking stack or experience with another production-grade kernel.
• Proficiency with debugging tools spanning kernel, network, and userspace (e.g., ftrace, perf, Wireshark/tcpdump, eBPF, gdb, and more).
• Experience bringing up new hardware from scratch — you have flashed bare-metal software on a microcontroller with JTAG, or bootstrapped a Linux kernel and rootfs on new hardware.
• Demonstrated track record of developing and optimizing device/peripheral drivers ideally for high-speed interfaces, or with advanced considerations like DMA and cache coherency.
• Understanding of major peripheral hardware interface standards (Ethernet, PCIe, I2C, SPI, etc.) — you can critically review a schematic, and debug these interfaces if needed.
• Experience with product security, OS/system hardening, and secure boot schemes.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

GNC ENGINEER - EMBEDDED CONTROLS, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)
SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.
The Starmind team is developing key technologies to power this satellite – massive solar power generation systems, active cooling, propulsion, and the highly reliable software stack that enables our vehicles to accomplish their mission safely and autonomously.
As an Embedded Controls Engineer on the Starmind Guidance, Navigation, and Control team (GNC) team, you will apply a strong expertise in dynamics and closed loop controls to achieve robust and precise pointing on satellites, payloads, propulsion systems, and mechanisms. This is not just an analysis role – you will be responsible for vehicle design trades, simulation, flight software implementation, and ultimately deploying and operating your features in space.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Design, analysis, implementation of electromechanical control systems such as solar array actuators, antenna gimbals, and high bandwidth active optics.
• Design, analysis, implementation of satellite attitude control and momentum management systems.
• Design, analysis, implementation of fluid and power system controls for the Starlink hall thrusters.
• Optimal state estimation as applied to mechanical alignment and attitude determination.
• Hardware performance specification and sizing, support for hardware iteration and firmware bringup, design qualification, automated production screening, and performance monitoring in the fleet.
• Development and maintenance of high fidelity simulations using C++, python, matlab, integration of those simulations into collaborative analysis tools.
• Implementation, validation, unit testing, and deployment of production software (C++) pertinent to the systems described above.
• Provide engineering and data review support for hardware development, network level performance monitoring.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor's degree in aerospace, physics or an engineering discipline.
• Software development experience in C++.
• Experience with design and analysis of closed loop control systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

SR. WIRELESS FIRMWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK MOBILE)
The Starlink Mobile program is working to provide global cellular connectivity from space. As a wireless firmware engineer, you will play a critical role in developing novel wireless signal processing algorithms, implementing optimized software for use on satellites and ground stations, debugging complex systems and performance issues, and developing production software. This is a unique position which will work closely with both wireless systems engineers and protocol firmware engineers to accelerate wireless PHY development and find solutions to interdisciplinary challenges. The ideal candidate will be equally comfortable with wireless signal processing algorithms and high-performance software development.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Design and implement physical layer (PHY) algorithms for satellite-based 4G/5G (LTE/NR) eNodeB/gNodeB.
• Develop optimized signal processing algorithms running on resource-constrained CPUs.
• Develop models and run simulations to analyze and validate overall system performance, including modem performance.
• Design, implement, test, maintain, and document the wireless PHY and MAC layers of the protocol stack.
• Identify and debug complex performance issues across the wireless PHY and MAC layers.
• Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews. Contribute to system dimensioning and algorithm design for next generation hardware.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor's, Master’s or PhD degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering or a STEM discipline.
• 5+ Years of experience with at least 1 of the following: wireless signal processing, modem systems design, wireless systems engineering, DSP (digital signal processing), or physical layer processing (L1).
• 5+ Years of C/C++ coding experience.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
• Familiarity with 3GPP 4G/5G (LTE/NR) physical layer design or other modern broadband OFDM waveforms such as WiMAX, 802.11 WiFi, DVB-S2, DVB-C, 5G NTN (non-terrestrial networks).
• Familiarity with forward error correction (FEC) coding concepts.
• Basic familiarity with MAC layer (medium access control, L2).
• Development and optimization of complex signal processing algorithms in both fixed and floating point.
• Familiarity with Linux command line use, git-based version control, and python programming.
• SDR (software defined radio) experience.
• Experience supporting products through the full release cycle including commercial deployment.
• Strong skills in debugging and performance optimization; exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
• Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay range:
Software Engineer/Senior: $160,000.00 - $225,000.00/per year
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock, stock options, or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:
• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.location: Maynard, Massachusetts, United States of America
requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Computer Engineering or related field with 8+ years of professional experience.
6+ years in low-level embedded C and C++ programming for physical hardware control.
5+ years development of embedded firmware on bare-metal systems and real-time operating systems (RTOS such as VxWorks, FreeRTOS, ThreadX, or similar).

Design, implementation and tuning real-time control systems (e.g., closed-loop feedback, PID control algorithms, or motion/thermal control loops) on embedded microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R).
Ability to work 100% onsite during the initial one-year onboarding period, (with hybrid flexibility available thereafter).
jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 11/29/2026

Meet the Team
Acacia (part of Cisco) is the industry market leader and pioneer in high-speed coherent optical transceivers and pluggable optical interconnects. Acacia’s revolutionary optical solutions are deployed across all major global hyperscale cloud providers and telecommunications networks, interconnecting data centers across metropolitan spans, thousands of kilometers of terrestrial fiber, and deep submarine links.
With the explosive growth of artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads driving unprecedented bandwidth requirements, Acacia’s high-speed optical transceivers are expanding into next-generation data center fabrics and high-performance compute clusters. In addition to powering deep-space optical communication systems, Acacia is leading the client-side optics market with breakthrough PAM4 DSP architectures, including industry-first 1.6T PAM4 DSP platforms.
Joining Acacia’s Software team in Maynard, MA means collaborating with world-class engineers to push the physical and algorithmic boundaries of optical networking.

Your Impact
As a Control Systems & Embedded Software Technical Leader, you will be a vital technical specialist responsible for designing and implementing high-speed closed-loop control systems, PID algorithms, and real-time embedded firmware that govern Acacia’s high-performance optical modules and transceivers.

In this hands-on engineering specialist role, you will:
• Design, tune, and optimize real-time closed-loop control algorithms (PID, motion control, temperature, and optical power stabilization) operating directly on bare-metal and RTOS microcontroller platforms.
• Develop highly efficient, compact embedded C/C++ firmware to configure, monitor, and calibrate hardware subsystems across ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R cores.
• Work closely with Hardware, Optics, and Calibration teams to bring up new boards, characterize feedback loops, and debug electro-optical interactions.
• Implement firmware state machines, low-level peripheral drivers, and high-reliability data/control paths.
• Own critical firmware features from algorithm simulation to production release, ensuring the highest reliability under demanding and optical conditions.

Minimum Qualifications (Objective Requirements)
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Computer Engineering or related field with 8+ years of professional experience.
• 6+ years in low-level embedded C and C++ programming for physical hardware control.
• 5+ years development of embedded firmware on bare-metal systems and real-time operating systems (RTOS such as VxWorks, FreeRTOS, ThreadX, or similar).
• Design, implementation and tuning real-time control systems (e.g., closed-loop feedback, PID control algorithms, or motion/thermal control loops) on embedded microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R).
• Ability to work 100% onsite during the initial one-year onboarding period, (with hybrid flexibility available thereafter).

Preferred Qualifications
• Development of control firmware for optical transceivers, laser controllers, optical amplifiers, or telecommunications hardware.
• Expertise with schematic reading, board bring-up, and lab instrumentation (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, optical spectrum analyzers).
• Development of multithreaded control-plane firmware, interrupt handlers, and complex finite state machines.
• Proficiency with version control (Git, Jira, Perforce) and test automation/data analysis scripting (Python, MATLAB).
• Background in semiconductor devices, hardware startups, sensor integration, or automated test platforms.

Senior Embedded Software Engineer – Networking Platforms
Location (Hybrid): Sunnyvale, CA
HPE Networking is a leader in AI-driven, next-generation networking solutions that help organizations modernize their infrastructure and securely connect people, applications, and data. Our networking portfolio powers some of the world's largest enterprise, cloud, and service provider environments through innovative hardware and software platforms.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Embedded Software Engineer to join our platform software team responsible for developing the low-level software that powers HPE-Juniper routing platforms. This is an excellent opportunity for engineers who enjoy working at the hardware-software boundary, building device drivers, programming network processors (NPUs) and ASICs, and enabling next-generation networking systems.
In this role, you will contribute to the development of high-performance networking platforms, working closely with hardware, firmware, and systems engineering teams to deliver reliable, scalable solutions for next-generation routing products.

What You'll Do
• Design, develop, and maintain embedded platform software and firmware for networking systems.
• Develop low-level software, device drivers, and system components for Linux-based networking platforms.
• Program and enable Network Processors (NPUs), ASICs, and other platform hardware.
• Participate in all phases of the software development lifecycle, including architecture, design, implementation, testing, debugging, and sustaining engineering.
• Develop functional specifications, software designs, and unit test plans.
• Bring up new hardware platforms and support board-level integration and validation.
• Troubleshoot complex hardware and software issues using advanced debugging techniques and tools.
• Collaborate closely with hardware, systems, firmware, and architecture teams to deliver high-quality networking products.
• Contribute to continuous improvements in software quality, performance, and reliability.

Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
• 10+ years of professional experience developing embedded software or firmware.
• Strong programming skills in C and C++.
• Extensive experience developing embedded software in Linux or Unix environments.
• Hands-on experience developing software for networking platforms, including routers or switches.
• Experience developing device drivers and system-level software.
• Experience bringing up new hardware platforms and supporting hardware validation.
• Strong debugging and problem-solving skills using software, hardware, and memory analysis tools.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to collaborate across cross-functional engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Job Description:
Designs, develops, troubleshoots, and debugs BIOS and platform firmware for new high-performance computing products. This role works close to the hardware, including processor initialization, chipset and board bring-up, hardware interfaces, system monitoring, networking-related platform enablement, and diagnostic tools. The developer identifies hardware and firmware compatibility issues, influences hardware design and validation, and helps deliver reliable firmware for complex server platforms.
Contributions include applying deep BIOS and platform-firmware expertise to solve complex technical problems, evaluate alternatives, and drive issues to closure across hardware and software boundaries. The role may act as a technical project lead, guide development approaches, and provide assistance to less experienced engineers. The developer exercises sound judgment, consults with cross-functional partners, and selects effective methods for accomplishing work and achieving program goals.

How You'll Make Your Mark
In this role, you will help bring up and enable complex HPC platforms by working across BIOS, hardware, operating system, and validation boundaries. You will contribute to early platform definition, firmware implementation, debug, and release readiness for systems where reliability, performance, and hardware integration are critical.
• Designs, develops, and maintains BIOS enhancements, updates, and programming changes for server and high-performance computing platforms.
• Assesses design, coding, integration, and validation activities based on product goals, platform architecture, hardware dependencies, and firmware requirements.

• Collaborates and communicates with management, internal teams, and outsourced development partners on firmware design status, project progress, technical risks, and issue resolution.
• Represents the system software engineering team through all phases of larger, more complex BIOS and platform-firmware development programs.
• Provides guidance and mentoring to less-experienced staff members.

• Minimum 15 years of experience in embedded software development.
• Minimum 10 years of experience in BIOS development.

• Expertise with BIOS technologies across multiple processor families, chipsets, and platform architectures.
• Expertise with UEFI firmware development, including platform initialization, driver development, debugging, and integration.
• Experience porting BIOS from a third-party vendor implementation to a proprietary platform.
• Experience with AMD, Nvidia or Intel
• Experience with Linux development environments, build tools, scripting, and firmware debug workflows.
• Strong analytical, assessment, and problem-solving skills, especially for complex hardware, firmware, and system integration issues.
• Experience designing software systems that run across multiple platform types and hardware configurations.
• Experience with firmware testing methodologies, including test-plan creation, debug workflows, automation, test scripts, and tools.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical issues, tradeoffs, and recommendations in English.
• Ability to communicate product architectures, firmware design proposals, technical tradeoffs, and recommended options effectively with engineering teams and management.

jobs.description:
About Etched
Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Job Summary
This role owns the accelerator software that turns our custom hardware into an inference system. You'll work across the stack from first power-on through inference execution: bringing CPUs and boards to life, moving data between host and device, and translating inference requests into low-level operations that execute directly on the accelerator. The work spans ASIC software, platform firmware, and host-side kernel and drivers. We hire engineers who are deep in one area and curious about the others.
This role spans across three work areas. You would specialize in one and contribute across the others as the team grows:
• ASIC Software — Build the software that runs directly on the accelerator. Work includes CPU initialization, RTOS, boot ROMs and bootloaders, MMU and IO drivers, ASIC/FW architecture and co-design, and on-device inference execution. Translate inference software requests into low-level device operations and scheduling decisions at nanosecond-level timescales to minimize overhead for highly interactive MoE and dense models.
• Platform Software — Build the microcontroller and FPGA firmware that brings our custom hardware from powered off to operational. Own areas including power sequencing, board bring-up, telemetry, firmware updates, thermal and power management, and fault detection and recovery. Work directly with hardware engineers through schematic design, bring-up, validation, and production.
• Host-side Kernel and Drivers — Build the software that connects the accelerator to the host and exposes it to the inference stack. Work includes Linux kernel and device drivers, PCIe and DMA, high-speed peripheral interfaces, memory management, FLR and virtualization/SR-IOV, and high-throughput, low-latency ring-buffer command flows.

You may be a good fit if you have
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
• Strong C/C++ and software engineering fundamentals.
• Experience building and debugging low-level software that interacts directly with hardware.
• Depth in one or more of firmware, embedded systems, device runtimes, operating systems, or kernel/driver development.
• Experience shipping software on real hardware into production.
• Familiarity with technologies such as ARM, PCIe, DMA, HBM, DRAM, Ethernet, UART, RTOS, or FPGA systems.
• Strong systems intuition around performance, concurrency, memory, reliability, and fault handling.

Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)
• Hardware bring-up experience on a new chip or board.
• Experience with boot ROMs, secure boot, MMUs, RTOS, or CPU initialization.
• Experience with PCIe virtualization, FLR, SR-IOV, DMA, ring buffers, or high-speed device communication.
• Experience building accelerator runtimes, schedulers, command processors, or other latency-critical execution systems.
• Experience using architecture details such as caching, memory hierarchy, or on-chip fabrics to make software decisions at nanosecond-level timescales.
• Experience solving ambiguous problems where the hardware and software architecture evolve together.
• Strong communication across firmware, hardware, architecture, kernel, and inference teams.

Benefits

• $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

• Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Principal Software Engineer, Embedded Linux
Job Location: San Jose, CA (This position requires a full-time, on-site presence in our San Jose, CA office)

Job ID: AI2497

Description
The SoC software team is responsible for creating the SDK for SiMa.ai’s MLSoC product line. This includes developing/porting OS, boot SW, device drivers, run time environment for multiple CPU subsystems that are part of SiMa.ai’s MLSoC(™), developing embedded Linux based applications and APIs for enabling end2end customer application flow utilizing different IO subsystems that are part of MLSoC.

Responsibilities:
We are looking for a seasoned software engineer who has experience developing OS device drivers, boot SW and key test applications in a Linux embedded environment. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of working in a high-performance team and has partnered with cross functional teams across multiple geographies. Key responsibilities include (but not limited to):
• Leverage IP SW from Synopsys and ARM and integrate into MLSoC™ SW environment
• Develop drivers for peripheral devices including Low and High speed interfaces for Linux
• Develop drivers and support for Docker and Hypervisor environments
• Test and verify Linux drivers and environment with Chip Virtualizers and Zebu emulators
• Hardware communication between multiple heterogeneous cores
• Configure Linux environments for different reference boards
• Modify and perform Yocto and eLxr/Debian builds for new functionality
• Provide SW to support HW MLSoC test validation team

Key Requirements:
• BS/MS in computer science with minimum 10 years of experience
• Hands-on experience developing firmware, boot code and SW using high performance 64 bit Arm processors
• Hands-on experience developing drivers for SPI, I2C, USB, PCIe, MIPI, Ethernet, eMMC
• Experience in working with silicon teams for pre-silicon verification, post-silicon bring-up and troubleshooting required
• Development experience with Embedded Linux (e.g. Yocto), Debian Linux and embedded RTOS (e.g. QNX) experience is highly desirable
• Experience with Docker and Hypervisors is highly desirable
• Experience of leveraging and developing on top of Open source software frameworks is highly desirable
• Good proficiency with C/C++
• Proven track record and experience building and delivering complex SW products

Personal attributes:
Can-do attitude. Strong team player. Curious, creative, and good at solving problems. Execution and results oriented. Self-driven, thinks big and is highly accountable. Good communication skills.
The annual salary for this position ranges from $203,800 - $315,900. The actual annual salary offered will depend on several factors, including - among others - job-related skills, experience, technical expertise, qualifications, work location, and business needs. The annual salary range for this position is subject to change and may be adjusted in the future.
In addition to base salary, this role is also eligible for private company equity, and a comprehensive package of employee benefits. Please note that the salary ranges listed for U.S. roles reflect base salary only and do not include equity or other forms of compensation.

jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
requirements: 5+ years of experience in firmware development
Experience with AI acceleration hardware
jobs.description:
Normal Computing | Build with Us
Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

The Role
As a Firmware Engineer at Normal, you will create low-level software to run on our SOC to provide an interface between our physics-inspired ASICs and higher software levels. You will have to develop code that runs on a microcontroller that provides an API layer for upper software levels to exercise our AI acceleration hardware. You will interface with the hardware and software design teams, understanding both the hardware and software architectures. You will debug in various prototyping and ASIC environments. For this role, you also have to specify and create the development environment. The through-line is your firmware expertise, applied to silicon and software stacks that compute differently from anything you have coded for before. This is a seat for a firmware engineer who wants their craft to compound rather than repeat.

What You Will Own
• Development of firmware for an embedded processor on an SOC: Create firmware to support an API that bridges higher-level software to the hardware layer.
• Work with software and hardware: Collaborate with software and hardware engineers to understand and specify the API requirements.
• Creation of the development environment: Acquire and configure appropriate tools to create the firmware, including compilers, simulators, and debuggers. Work across multiple development environments including software simulation, RTL simulation, and physical hardware.
• Verification of the firmware to a production level: Develop a verification and stress test plan and environment to guarantee production quality of the firmware

What Makes You a Great Fit
• 5+ years of experience in firmware development
• Specification and creation of a firmware development environment for a shipping product
• Expertise in various firmware languages and target architectures
• Excellent written and spoken communication skills

Bonus Points
• RISC-V experience

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about FPGA prototyping? Are you interested in pushing the boundaries of innovation to make FPGA prototypes faster and more efficient? Can you work in a fast-paced environment that requires coordination between many teams across geographies and resolving sophisticated problems daily? If so, we are looking for hardworking engineers who will craft FPGA prototypes of our next generation GPUs and SOCs on standard FPGA prototyping platforms.
We are now looking for a Senior FPGA Prototyping Engineer to join our Emulation team onsite in Santa Clara, CA.

What you'll be doing:
• Build FPGA prototypes by making RTL FPGA-friendly, partitioning the design and taking it through synthesis and place and route.
• Improve performance of the prototype, analyze timing and generate bit streams.
• Bring up the design on FPGA prototyping platforms and indulge in problem solving.
• Release the prototype to the customers and support them when they face problems.
• You are expected to understand the design and implementation, define the configurations, develop/modify the bringup and testing infrastructure and verify the correctness of the design.
• Good coordination with architects, designers, verification engineers, and SW teams will be needed to accomplish your tasks.

What we need to see:
• BS (or equivalent experience) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields with 12+ years of experience, or MS with 10+ years of proven experience in FPGA prototyping.
• Good understanding of FPGA prototyping architecture, devices, flows and tools.
• Experience in backend flows of FPGA Prototyping - Synthesis, P&R and Timing closure, with emphasis on Synopsys Protocompiler or Siemens VPS and Xilinx Vivado
• Exposure to ASIC design and verification tools (VCS or equivalent, Verdi, GDB).
• Knowledge of Verilog, System Verilog and digital design concepts.
• Good debugging and problem solving skills.
• Hands on experience with lab FPGA debug methodologies, tools (Identify or ChipScope), and lab debug equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers).

Ways to stand out from the crowd:
• Scripting knowledge (Perl/shell/Tcl) is desired.
• Good documentation, communication and interpersonal skills.
• Experience with memory bring up of Memory (LPDDR5/6, DDR5/6), CXL/PCIE and/or high speed I/F such as USB4/3 is desirable
• Prior experience with hardware emulation or prototyping (Synopsys HAPS or Siemens ProFPGA) of a high-performance processor or SOC is a plus.
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself over two decades. Our invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can tackle, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human imagination and intelligence. Make the choice to join us today!
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
196,000 USD – 310,500 USD for Level 5; and 232,000 USD – 368,000 USD for Level 6.
You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

jobs.description:
Job Description

About the Role
Renesas is seeking a Principal FPGA Emulation & Prototyping Engineer to build and own the FPGA-based platforms that emulate our mixed-signal power ASICs before silicon. Working shoulder to shoulder with our silicon RTL and DSP architects, you will bring their designs up on FPGA to validate real-time digital, mixed-signal, and power-control architectures pre-silicon — proving out control loops, catching RTL issues early, and de-risking tape-out.
These FPGA platforms are emulation vehicles, not production hardware. Success is measured by how faithfully and how fast they reproduce the target silicon: functional equivalence to the golden ASIC RTL, real-time (or near-real-time) performance for closed-loop power and DSP validation, and deep visibility for pre-silicon debug.

What You'll Do
• Partner closely with silicon RTL and DSP architects to bring ASIC designs up on FPGA — advising on FPGA-ability and turning architectural intent into a working, real-time emulation platform.
• Adapt ASIC RTL for FPGA emulation while preserving functional equivalence to the golden design — handling clock-gating conversion, memory/SRAM macro mapping, reset and initialization schemes, tri-state/bus conversion, and stubbing or modeling of analog/mixed-signal blocks.
• Map designs onto the FPGA fabric to fit and to hit emulation speed — steering resource inference (DSP/multiplier slices, block vs. distributed memory), clocking, and pipelining so the design achieves the real-time performance the validation requires.
• Build the real-time environment around the digital core: model or interface to the analog and power stages (ADC/DAC/PWM, gate drivers, plant/converter models), including hardware-in-the-loop with real or emulated power hardware where needed.
• Develop deep pre-silicon debug and visibility — logic analysis, long-run waveform capture, triggering, and assertions — and enable firmware/software co-development ahead of silicon.
• Define and continuously improve the emulation methodology, RTL/FPGA-ability guidelines, flows, and automation (TCL/Python).
• Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, lead reviews, and drive emulation and tooling decisions across the silicon and systems teams.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications
• Extensive FPGA design and implementation experience (typically 10+ years), including a track record of FPGA prototyping or emulation of ASIC/SoC designs.
• Expert-level RTL design in SystemVerilog and/or VHDL, with deep familiarity working from ASIC-style RTL.
• Deep understanding of FPGA internal architecture and primitives — DSP/multiplier slices, block and distributed RAM, carry chains, and clocking — and a proven ability to map designs onto these resources to fit large ASIC RTL and reach real-time emulation performance (memory/SRAM macro mapping, DSP inference, clock-enable conversion, control-set and fanout management).
• Hands-on experience adapting ASIC RTL for FPGA: clock-gating conversion, memory macro replacement, reset schemes, tri-state conversion, and multi-clock/CDC handling.
• Strong command of the full FPGA implementation flow — synthesis, place-and-route, timing analysis, and constraint development (XDC/SDC) — on large Xilinx and/or Intel (Altera) devices, using Vivado and/or Quartus.
• Hardware bring-up and debug experience: in-system logic analysis (ILA/SignalTap), lab instrumentation, and long-run pre-silicon debug.
• Proficiency scripting for automation (TCL, Python).
• Demonstrated technical leadership — mentoring, reviews, and driving cross-team technical decisions.
• BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

Preferred Qualifications
• Real-time, hardware-in-the-loop emulation and modeling of analog/mixed-signal and power stages (ADC/DAC/PWM interfaces, plant/converter models).
• Understanding of digital power-conversion control and mixed-signal systems — converter topologies, control loops, PWM/PFM, and magnetics — to build faithful models and validate power-control architectures.
• FPGA DSP implementation and real-time emulation of DSP datapaths: FIR/IIR/CIC filters, interpolation/decimation, FFT, FEC, including high-throughput techniques such as folding/unfolding.
• Experience with commercial FPGA prototyping platforms such as Synopsys HAPS, Cadence Protium, or Siemens Veloce.
• Model-based design with Simulink and/or Xilinx System Generator.
• High-speed interface experience: JESD204B, PCIe, 1G/10G Ethernet, Aurora.
• ASIC design or tape-out exposure, including DFT/scan considerations in emulation.
• Ability to architect and build a custom in-house FPGA prototyping platform — board architecture, high-speed PCB design, signal integrity, and bring-up — a plus as we may develop our own hardware in the future.
• Embedded/microcontroller and firmware co-development experience (C/assembly); MATLAB, C/C++.

Job Description:
Altera is enabling the future of programmable solutions that power innovation across AI, cloud, communications, industrial, aerospace, and defense applications. We are looking for a talented FPGA IP Software Development Engineer to join our engineering team and help develop next-generation FPGA-based platforms and embedded solutions.

Position Summary
As an FPGA IP Software Development Engineer, you will play a key role in designing, integrating, validating, and debugging FPGA-based systems for embedded, networking, and acceleration applications. This role is primarily focused on FPGA RTL development and system integration, including PCIe, High-Speed Interfaces (HPS), External Memory Interfaces (EMIF), and Ethernet IPs.
You will work closely with hardware and software teams on FPGA HW/SW co-development, system bring-up, debugging, and optimization of complex FPGA-based products, including SmartNICs, embedded platforms interacting with GPU and ARM HPS-based solutions.
The ideal candidate has strong FPGA design expertise, experience integrating complex IP subsystems, and an interest in collaborating across hardware and software domains.

Key Responsibilities

FPGA Design & Integration
• Design, develop, integrate, and validate RTL for FPGA-based systems and platforms.
• Implement and integrate FPGA subsystems various I/0 Technologies (PCIe, EMIF, Ethernet & networking IPs) and on-board ARM Hard Processor Systems (HPS)
• Support FPGA system architecture, performance optimization, and debug activities.

HW/SW Co-Development
• Collaborate with software and application teams on FPGA HW/SW co-design and integration.
• Support board bring-up, system-level validation, and debugging.
• Develop software abstractions, drivers, and frameworks that enable FPGA acceleration solutions.
• Partner with cross-functional teams to optimize end-to-end system performance.

• SmartNIC solutions
• Embedded computing platforms (Physical AI/Robotics) with GPU
• ARM-based FPGA systems
• Communication and data center acceleration solutions
• Participate in architecture discussions and technical reviews.
• Support product deployment and customer-facing technical investigations as needed.

Process & Innovation

jobs.description:
We live in a mobile and device-driven world where knowledge of the physical world around us is essential. Apple is meeting those needs as robustly and creatively as possible, and we're looking for people who want to help us achieve that commitment. The Imaging and Sensing Incubation team develops design solutions for user experiences and new technologies across iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, MacBooks, and more. Our team creates early-stage hardware systems integrating cameras, non-vision sensors like IMUs, magnetometers, accelerometers, microphones, and ambient light sensors, including systems that enable Apple Intelligence features. We offer a collaborative, inclusive, hands-on environment that cultivates engineering excellence, creativity, and innovation. Apple's Incubation team is seeking an FPGA Design Engineer to bring hardware systems to life, systems essential to delivering future products, features, and Apple Intelligence capabilities. You'll develop FPGA-based platforms from architecture through hardware bring-up, building multi-sensor acquisition and processing systems and influencing hardware, algorithm, and system design decisions. You'll have the autonomy to make design decisions and see their impact in working hardware. Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for engineers to help achieve that mission.
The Compute Silicon & Manufacturing Engineering (CSME) organization within SCHIE is responsible for design, development, manufacturing and packaging of Microsoft's state-of-the-art computer chips, notably the Azure Cobalt. jobs.description:
The Models, Quantum, and Silicon (MQS) Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is a multi-disciplinary team of scientists, engineers, and technicians, on a mission to develop a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
We are looking for an FPGA Engineer to contribute to our quantum control platform. As a part of the control stack team, you will develop and integrate RTL designs and embedded software with an eye towards overcoming novel challenges in experimental quantum computing, such as high-throughput device characterization & calibration, or enabling real-time quantum error correction protocols. The ideal candidate will help us work backwards from our broader experimental goals, driving improvements to our control platform at the hardware/software interface while ensuring that high-level requirements (e.g. latency, bandwidth, resource utilization) are met.
This position is on-site at our lab, located on the Caltech campus in Pasadena, CA.
Work/Life Balance
At the MQS CQC, we understand that developing quantum computing technology is a marathon, not a sprint. Mental and physical wellness is encouraged within our team and throughout AWS. The work/life integration within Amazon encourages a culture where employees work hard and have ownership over their downtime. We are exploring more structured wellness elements including meditation scheduling, running group meet-ups, and a culture of sharing wellness tips.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We are committed to the growth and development of every member of the Center for Quantum Computing. You will receive career-growth-minded management and mentorship from a software and science team, and also have the opportunity to participate in Amazon's mentorship programs. You will work closely with quantum research scientists and have opportunities to learn about quantum computing technology and contribute to the development of scientific software for quantum computing at AWS.
Inclusive and Diverse Culture
Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and we host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 16 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.
Key job responsibilities
• Work with stakeholders to understand and refine hardware/software requirements.
• Propose architectural or micro-architectural updates to our control platform to meet requirements.
• Implement RTL subsystems in Verilog or SystemVerilog.
• Develop embedded software in C, C++ or Rust for high-performance near-real-time tasks.
• Verify & validate designs, both in simulation and in bench-top / real-world conditions.
• Ensure new features are successfully integrated into our Python-based experimental software stack.
We are looking for candidates with strong engineering principles, resourcefulness and a bias for action, superior problem-solving and excellent communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. As a member of a research organization, you will have the opportunity to work on new ideas and stay abreast of the field of experimental quantum computation.
A day in the life
The majority of your time will be spent on projects that extend the functional capabilities or performance of our existing control platform. This requires working backwards from the needs of our science staff in the context of our larger experimental roadmap. You will translate hardware and software requirements into design proposals balancing implementation complexity against time-to-delivery. Once a design proposal has been reviewed and accepted, you will drive the implementation and coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure a smooth roll out. Because many high-level experimental goals have cross-cutting requirements, you’ll often work closely with other software or hardware engineers on the team.
About the team
